This is a legislative requirement that is carried out every three years. All employees who have not been enrolled onto a Pension scheme in the last 12 months will be automatically re-enrolled into a relevant pension scheme (OSPS, USS, NEST, NHS) according to their contract type and grade.
The Pensions team will contact the affected employees in advance to let them know that they will be re-enrolled.
Testing will be completed in collaboration with the Payroll team and agreement will need to be reached about when the testing can take place.

This process may be a candidate for a Standard Change as we do not configure the system, the re-enrolment periods are updated automatically.

Auto Enrolment re-enrolment is a legislative process that must be carried out every three years. Further details can be found on the Pensions Regulator website - https://www.thepensionsregulator.gov.uk/en/employers/re-enrolment
For the main University, the exercise is carried out in June and previous exercises have been carried out in 2016, 2019 and 2022. The next exercise is due in June 2025.
For Linacre College the exercise is carried out a year later and in July. Previous exercises were completed in 2017 and 2020. The next exercise is due in July 2023.

llege the exercise is carried out a year later and in July. Previous exercises were completed in 2017 and 2020. The next exercise is due in July 2023. The Re-Enrolment period is set against the relevant Pay groups (20 and 21 for the main University and 60 for Linacre). This will be updated automatically once the latest exercise is completed but it is always worth checking that the periods have been updated as expected.
To check the settings navigate to:- Payroll Dashboard > UK Tax Rates > General > Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters. Select 'Auto-Enrolment' and then choose 'Pay Groups'.

To send a control report to the Report Centre, select the Ellipses button and click Send to Report Centre.
There is an option to send all of the control reports to the report centre, select the Generate All Reports button in the top right-hand corner.
The following control reports are available:
Nett Pay Curr-Prev Exceptions Report:

elect the Generate All Reports button in the top right-hand corner.
The following control reports are available:
Nett Pay Curr-Prev Exceptions Report: This report compares employees nett pay in the current period with employees’ nett pay in the previous period.
Payroll Exceptions Report:
The Payroll Exceptions Report shows the top 10 earners, bottom 10 earners, payroll observation messages, and the control summary. Observation messages detail all errors and warnings for the current payroll period.
Payroll Controls (PAYB141) report:
This report ensures that the payroll is balances from the previous payroll period detailing any amendments which have impacted on employee cumulative details. Amendments can be generated due to:
The input of employee P45 details.
Employees moving in and out of the pay group.
Cancellation of previous historical payments in the current tax year.
Detailed Amendments Report
This report breaks down the amendments column in the payroll controls report by employee.
Gross to Nett Report
This report provides the gross to nett breakdown by employee.

The Casual Payment Submission spreadsheet was created as a direct result of the project ‘Ensuring legal compliance for casual workers’ in 2016.
Responsibility for creating casual worker records was devolved to departments and introduced the mandatory use of an Excel spreadsheet to submit worker payments to Payroll. The spreadsheet supports the capture of weekly working hours for Tier 4 workers. The removal of paper and the submission of encrypted timesheets electronically will lead to improved efficiency and information security.
The spreadsheet was developed by Software Solutions (David Hickman) and contains validation rules to ensure data is entered correctly and macros to convert the data entered into a format that can be loaded directly into the payroll module.
The workbook contains hidden sheets, rows and columns and is protected to prevent the validation rules and macros from being changed or deleted accidentally.
Full instructions on how to edit the spreadsheet can be found in the Technical specification document.

ros from being changed or deleted accidentally.
Full instructions on how to edit the spreadsheet can be found in the Technical specification document. There are two versions of the spreadsheet:
Casual Payment Submission Spreadsheet Department use – for all departments except TSS. This version of the spreadsheet contains all relevant pay codes for departmental use and validates entries against the CASUAL and CASTCH bucket posts.
Casual Payment Submission Spreadsheet TSS.
This version of the spreadsheet contains the pay codes applicable to TSS and validates entries against the specific TSS bucket posts.
All other validation rules and macros are the same.
In 2022 online time sheeting is being piloted. One workgroup in the Physics department are submitting timesheets online. It is hoped that this will be implemented across the whole University in time thus removing the need for the Submission spreadsheet.

The change process applicable at the time of the change should be followed. The current process is to create a change request in OSM which is approved by the relevant approver. Ideally, the change should be approved prior to being put into QA testing.
The HRIS Functional Analysis Team are responsible for setting up new grades & points and amending existing grades & points.
If a new grade is being created and the Full Time Hours value for the grade is not present in the list of ‘FTE Hours’ in the database, a new value will need to be created. This can either be done via a separate change or added as a separate element to the current change. For information on how to add a new FTE Hours value, refer to the document How To – View and Maintain Reference Data.
Note that, in some cases, it may be necessary to move employees onto a new grade or point. For example, the lowest scale point (4) was removed from Apprentice Grade 01A in Feb 2018 as it fell below the minimum Living Wage. Employees who were appointed to this grade/scale therefore needed to be moved onto the next highest scale point (5).

Pay Code Knowledge Article
Background
By default, all Pay Codes are returned to employees in the Timesheet Entry and Absence Entry screens. Pay Code Groups can be used to tailor the list of pay codes returned to employee and managers when inputting and viewing data.
Pay Code Groups can be assigned to the employee and/or their appointment.
Pay code groups are assigned to Managers either by System users or Work Groups. In these cases, the system user level configuration takes precedence over the work groups level.
The default manager configuration is:
No Pay Code Grouping applied

System User Level/Organisational Role
Pay Code groups which are assigned at System User/Organisational roles level take precedence over the Work Groups.
Within site settings, the Manager Before Org Roles Access decides if an Organisation role or Username take precedence.
3. Employees Work Group
The personalised groups assigned to an employee’s work group dictates codes. As an example, If a manager has employees in various work groups, the list of pay codes available will also vary.
Manager and Administrator input applies to the following screens:
Timesheet Input
Absence Details
Time Exceptions
Record Absence Details (back-office)
Maintain hours (back-office)
Pay Code Access Groups are required for Accrual Balances to enable staff to record time against specific pay codes.
Formatting of the Group Codes and Descriptions
There is a standard format for Access Group Codes and Descriptions:-
For Employees the Code is Prefixed with 'EM' and the Description with 'Employee' followed by further details e.g. Code = EMFX6+, Description = Employee (Grade 6 & above)

Does the change need to be raised through a particular route or by a particular person/team? Are there any actions which need to be taken or considered prior to processing in the HRIS Support Centre?
New Pension Schemes
The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for requesting the creation of new pension schemes.
Pensions should discuss the requirements for the new pension scheme with Payroll. Payroll must then complete a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and send it through to the HRIS Support Centre, together with details of any new or amended pay codes which are required to support the new scheme. The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request for a new pension scheme as a change within OSM.

The Pensions team will likely give a few months of advance warning when a new scheme needs to be set up, so that there is sufficient time to set it up in a test environment and check that the payroll and reporting outputs for the new scheme are all correct.
Changes to Existing Schemes
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to existing pension schemes.
Pensions must raise a support-desk call to the Functional Analysis team and provide details of the changes to be made. If the changes are for contribution rates, Pensions must supply the official “schedule of contributions” from the scheme provider showing the new rates and their effective date.
The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with Payroll and Pensions to test the changes before making them live.
Changes to the State Pension Age (SPA)
The Pensions team is responsible for requesting changes to the State Pension Age.
The State Pension Age (also called the “State Retirement Age”) is the age at which an individual can begin claiming their state pension, based on their gender and date of birth. It is set by the UK government, and is periodically revised.

The HRIS Functional Analysis team will process the request as a change within OSM, and must liaise with Pensions to test the updated State Pension Age parameters before making them live.
Changes to Auto-Enrolment

Diversity and disability data are recorded and displayed in a variety of places in the system. This data is restricted and can only be viewed by the employee via Employee Self Service (ESS) and by central teams such as Systems Support, HR Analytics and the EDU team.
Diversity and disability data are collected from all applicants via the online application forms. If an applicant is appointed, the details entered on their application form are automatically inserted into the employee record. The employee can update their data via ESS at any time (and via the onboarding checklist if applicable).
The questions relating to Diversity and Disability data are included in the individual application form profiles. Where changes are required to the reference data, labels or help text, these must be made on each form.

Payroll calendar
On the Employee Self Service landing page, the date of the next Pay Day and the number of days to go is displayed in the ‘Important Dates’ section (see below).
On the actual Pay Day, the legend says ‘today’. The day after Pay Day the next date is displayed.
A separate calendar is required for the calendar year for each Pay Group paid through payroll. At the present time we have calendars for pay groups 20 and 21.
In December each year new calendars will need to be created for the following year. It is not possible to overwrite an existing calendar to add dates for the following year so new calendars must be created. There does not appear to be any way to ‘direct’ the Pay Day view to a specific calendar, it seems to rely on the year in the SYSDATE matching the year on the Calendar. Option 2 – The day after December’s pay day, create new calendars for the forthcoming year and delete the calendars for the outgoing year. NB: The Next Pay Date section in the Portal will be blank until the new calendars have been created.

The restructure tool
The Post Restructuring Tool is software within Core Personnel which enables us to move high volumes of employees between different areas of the Organisational hierarchy.
Organisational hierarchy changes currently occur annually (PRAS organisation changes). However minor departmental restructures can occur at any time and often Data Services assist with these changes.
The tool automates a number of tasks that would otherwise need to be completed manually. The tool can be run in two modes;
Update Existing Contracts: – agreed method since 2017.
Retains existing Appointment ID and creates a new post and sequence.
Create New Contracts: – no longer used.
Creates a new Appointment id, post and sequence
It can be run at Employee, Post or Organisational level which means longer term there is the potential to use the tool for correcting errors on individual employee post/appt records. Potentially eliminating the need for users a having to create Staff Requests to correct hierarchy details on post/appt.

Adding a new UDF UDFs are ‘forms’ that can be used to store additional information which cannot be recorded anywhere else in the Personnel module. There is a standard template that cannot be altered although the field descriptions and content can be configured.
UDFs can be held at Appointment, Person (employee) or Recruitment level. This is determined via the Advanced settings when creating a UDF.
Person and Appointment level UDFs are accessed within the employee record in People Management in the User Defined Field section. Recruitment UDFs are less common and relate to additional sections added to the online Application Forms. The Application Form with inbuilt supporting statement has one UDF and the Apprenticeship Application form has three. These provide additional sections that could not be included any other way.
Each UDF is assigned a Reference Code and Description when it is first created.
The reference code is restricted to 6 characters (alpha). It is used for reporting purposes to identify the relevant data items. It is not displayed in the UDF.
The Description is displayed within the UDF in the Select Detail or Selection menus as applicable. There is a 40 character limit for the Description.

The Description is displayed within the UDF in the Select Detail or Selection menus as applicable. There is a 40 character limit for the Description. There are 12 Fields available. UDFs are configured in the Portal via People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects.

Changing a UDF Making amendments to UDFs is technically straight forward; However, great care must be taken as existing data will not automatically feed through to the data which has already been entered. This is because data is entered against an Item Number generic across all UDFs rather than against a field specific to that UDF. Please read the information below before proceeding.
Adding a new List Item to an existing list
Adding a new List Item to an existing list will not have any impact on existing data.
You can also amend the order in which the list items are displayed by re-entering the entire list or swapping items around.
Editing existing List Items:
Any changes made will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. However the UDF itself will not update automatically on the individual records and an error message will be displayed whenever the UDF is opened. To correct this the individual UDF records must be updated to re-select the edited item. This is a manual process as each UDF needs to be opened within every affected employee record, the updated field(s) reselected and the changes saved.

This is a manual process as each UDF needs to be opened within every affected employee record, the updated field(s) reselected and the changes saved. For this reason changes can only be made with agreement from all affected parties and where a plan is in place to correct the employee records.
List Items - The preferred approach is to add a new list item, update the affected records to select the ‘new’ list item and then untick the active indicator against the ‘old’ list item.
Example:
Right to Work List item ‘EEA Family Permit’ was changed to ‘EEA Family Permit (6 months)’ in Jan18. A new list item was added for the new description, the affected employee records were updated to select the ‘new’ description and the ‘old’ list item showing the previous description was made inactive.
Editing existing Field items:
Any changes to the Description will apply to all existing records where the edited field(s) have previously been selected. Unlike the List items the Field items will update automatically and no changes will be required to the individual records. However, any reports containing the edited UDF will need to be updated as the column headers will refer to the previous Field Item Description.

Data Warehouse Most UDFs are migrated into the Data Warehouse and split out into individual tables according to their code. There are then views built which translate the underlying columns (text1, text2 etc) into their actual headings. If you are changing the structure of a UDF (introducing a new field, changing the heading) there will be changes required to the warehouse. If you are replacing a UDF with a new version with a new name then all of the tables in the warehouse will need to be rebuilt. You must inform the HR Analytics Team, or the HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager, of the changes being made.
Interfaces
UDFs are rarely used within interface files but information in the Right to Work UDF is taken by the following interfaces:
CoreHR to Access Databases ‘staff including casuals’ interface (Interface Staging PROGID_170), which sends email to HRIS Support with subject lines following this pattern: Interface Staging: req=hris/pcapps/staff ref=%ID% status=SUCCESS.
CoreHR to EAP interface (Interface Staging PROGID to be confirmed), which sends Right to Work data for all staff to the Examiner Appointments and Payments system, transforming the CoreHR data into “Right to Work = TRUE/FALSE” values.

ht to Work data for all staff to the Examiner Appointments and Payments system, transforming the CoreHR data into “Right to Work = TRUE/FALSE” values. NB!! Rules have been built into these interfaces to extract the data from the RTW2 UDF. Any proposed changes to the UDF or the description of the data labels within it will need to be fed back to the SSM-BITE team before the changes are made, so that the interfaces can be modified as necessary to continue picking up the required RTW information.
This is particularly important as UDFs are set up against generic Name/Description/Types, e.g. Reference Code, Item1, User Field1. Changes to the structure of a specific UDF need to be explicitly communicated to the SSM-BITE team so that they can ensure that the necessary parameters are in place in the interface to pick up the data from the modified UDF.
Affected Reports

There will almost always be reports affected by a change to a UDF as there is normally at least one accompanying report with that UDF. However this would depend on the UDF being updated as there is not one “UDF” report, rather they are reported on separately using the UDF “Reference Code” to only return data of a specific UDF type within any given report.

UDF” report, rather they are reported on separately using the UDF “Reference Code” to only return data of a specific UDF type within any given report. Any changes to UDFs (including moving from one UDF to another for the same purpose – e.g. ‘RTW’ to ‘RTW2’) will need to be reflected in the report. In a similar way to interfaces, the reports will still run but the data they return is likely to be out of sequence or not make sense if a report is not updated, and will therefore return inaccurate information.

Thank you for your email request for the deletion of your University of Oxford e-Recruitment on-line account. Background
The onboarding checklist is based on the items gathered in the paper New Starter Data Collection form and is intended to replace this form, providing a more secure and efficient method for gathering the information.
On/Offboarding checklists are configured via the Social Hub configuration widget which has been added to the Administrator Dashboard.
Following a successful pilot the onboarding checklist was launched to the whole University from 1 November 2023. Through the use of Staff Groups the checklist was released to New Starters, Rehires and New Appointments (NAA, NAT, NC, CIGI, CIGD) and applied to appointments which started on or after 1 November 2023.
Checklists are made up of a variety of different items configured to form tasks. These include:
Input items – standard items – e.g. Bank details

2023.
Checklists are made up of a variety of different items configured to form tasks. These include:
Input items – standard items – e.g. Bank details UDFs – Person level UDFs can be added to the checklist for completion by the employee. In all cases a new UDF is created. NB: Appointment level UDFs are not available but we have raised this with Access Group
Surveys – these are ‘questionnaires’ specifically configured by us mostly to gather data required for Appointment UDFs
Custom Forms – provide information e.g. A welcome message from the Pro VC/HR Director and links to staff handbooks
Onboarding tasks apply to all appointments that meet the criteria specified in the staff groups where the start date is on or after the activation date.
Exceptions
When an appointment is commenced on or after 1 November 2023, onboarding tasks will be assigned even if the effective date of the appointment is before the activation date. Raised with Access Group case # 64406103.
Where tasks have previously been assigned and completed, a further qualifying appointment may not result in the tasks being assigned again. However, any tasks that were not previously assigned and completed will be created and assigned to the employee. E.g. an individual moving from a non clincial to a clincal role will be assigned the tasks required for clinical appointments.

signed to the employee. E.g. an individual moving from a non clincial to a clincal role will be assigned the tasks required for clinical appointments. When activating onboarding, the system will create and assign tasks for all active employees that meet the criteria specified in the staff groups. It will then mark all tasks as completed where the appointment start date is before the activation date.
Exceptions
When onboarding was re-set a few examples were identified where the tasks has been automatically completed incorrectly. Raised with Access Group case # 64406103.
Staff Grouping
Staff groups control (restrict) which questions are presented to each employee. There are a large number of criteria to choose from when creating Staff Groups including, Category and Sub Category, Appointment Reason, Department and Division. In preparation for the wider roll out new staff groups were created to cater for Casual workers and TSS workers plus the New appointment reason codes.
The full details of Staff Groups can be found in the Configuration document.
Multiple staff group restrictions can be applied to a task. Each task on the checklist has at least one staff group restriction assigned.
A matrix showing the allocation of questions per staff group can be found here.

ation of questions per staff group can be found here.
Automatic notifications
Automatic notifications have been enabled as part of the wider roll out. The notifications are generated once a week on Sunday and sent to every employee with outstanding task/s to remind them to log in and complete them.
A separate notification can also be sent to employees whose appointment start date is within the two-week period following the notification date (not activated).
Apart from configuring the email there is no flexibility within the automated notifications and there is no way to specify/restrict who receives a notification.

Social activity is optional for departments to use. This section only appears in the Social Hub if an HR admin has added a message to the employee via the employee record.

The Active Roles Web Interface is used by HR Systems to manage access to the HR Reporting environments. Individuals are added to Active Directory (“AD”) groups, and the groups are granted read-only access to folders and sub-folders within the HR Reporting environments. Which AD groups are granted access to which folders/sub-folders is determined by consultation, usually within the Functional Analysis or HR Analytics teams, but often with input from the HR Systems business change advisors.
Note: all users must login to the HR Reporting environments via CONNECT. Users with CONNECT managed desktops will be logged in automatically, but those without CONNECT managed desktops must be set up with a “Global” CONNECT account. The Functional Analysis team are responsible for the creation of these accounts for users of HR Reporting.
Only a small number of people within HR Systems have access to the Active Roles Web Interface to view and manage the AD groups; the site itself is managed by the Microsoft Platform Services Team (“MPST”). Balances Overview
Within Time Management each appointment requires an associated Balance which determines how the annual leave for the appointment will be calculated. The Balance can draw on a range of parameters, dependent on the settings, including: Holiday Schemes, Long Service Schemes, timesheet hours and the current appointment.
Departments are responsible for assigning the appropriate Balance to each appointment via People Management, but cannot view the underlying Balance settings. It is therefore important that the Balances are correctly configured and appropriately named, so that HR administrators can easily identify the correct option and audit their appointments for errors.

orrectly configured and appropriately named, so that HR administrators can easily identify the correct option and audit their appointments for errors. Before further balances are created, it is recommended that the new setting providing the option to connect the balance to the appointment FTE Hours is explored. If Balances no longer need to be specific to appointments sharing the same FTE Hours value, the total number of Balances could be significantly reduced and HR Admins would be able to apply the same Balance to support staff and academic-related staff.
New Balance Settings = Advanced parameters > Company Holiday Entitlement
Fields: Link ‘Default Hours to Personnel’ & ‘Personnel Default Hours Divisor
Tweaking of the Entitlements per Balance is also required when these settings are in use, so that one Balance can be linked to multiple Long Service Schemes.
Identifying when a new Balance is required
To reduce the risk of departments assigning the wrong Balance and to minimise the central overhead of maintaining PeopleXD-Time, new Balances (and any associated config items) should only be created when necessary.
To determine if a new Balance and/or associated config items are required, follow the Balance decision tree.

Is the balance likely to be required long-term and used by multiple employees and does it warrant the additional maintenance overhead or complexity? If bespoke Balances or Holiday Schemes covering only a small number of appointments are frequently requested, it may become necessary to apply some sort of threshold. Universal leave year Vs Personal leave year
Accrual Balances can be configured in two ways to cater for the common annual leave arrangements used by paid as claimed-style appointments:
Universal leave year – linked to a set leave year, such as the University standard leave year which runs 1st October – 30th September.
Personal Leave Year – Leave year determined per appointment, e.g. using the appointment start date as the leave year start.
Accrual Balances & Pay Codes

rsonal Leave Year – Leave year determined per appointment, e.g. using the appointment start date as the leave year start.
Accrual Balances & Pay Codes Leave which is accrued is managed through timesheets. For the balance to function correctly and to allow staff to record leave taken, Pay Codes need to be correctly configured. Unlike Entitlement Balances, which share pay codes, it is likely each Accrual Balance will require its own set of Pay Codes including:
At least one Accrual Pay Code which accrues leave e.g. 107 PAID AS CLAIMED PAYMENT
At least one Holiday Pay Code which records leave taken e.g. 4231 CAS HOLIDAY PAY (HRS)
Pay Codes should be created before attempting to configure an Accrual Balance. Bespoke Pay Code Access Groups will be required to enable the appropriate staff to record time against these pay codes.
Long Service Scheme (for Accrual Balances)
A Long Service Scheme can be linked to an Accrual Balance, but this is optional and Accrual Balances will function without a scheme.
Long Service schemes should only be linked to Accrual Balances that follow a universal leave year, they cannot not be used with Accrual Balances that follow a personal calendar.
Entitlement Balances - Background

s that follow a universal leave year, they cannot not be used with Accrual Balances that follow a personal calendar.
Entitlement Balances - Background An entitlement Balance provides the employee with an annual leave allowance to use during their leave year. The amount of entitlement the system issues is calculated by drawing on several factors: the settings within the Balance itself, certain appointment settings and where applicable, the associated configuration items (e.g. Holiday Scheme).
The appointment settings impacting the entitlement are:
Contracted hours/multiplier – part-timers get a pro rata entitlement
Start /end date – e.g. those starting mid leave year get a pro rata entitlement
Continuous service start date – factored into the long service entitlement (if applicable)
Balances are assigned in days for full time staff and hours for part time staff. In this context full time staff means staff who work the standard days every week, according to their grade e.g. 7.5 hours per day for Grade 6 and above. If an employee works different hours each day then the annual leave balance should be assigned in hours. In this scenario public holidays and fixed closure days will be assigned the actual hours due to be worked on those days.
Most balance settings will be the same across all entitlement Balances, the settings which differ are:

he actual hours due to be worked on those days.
Most balance settings will be the same across all entitlement Balances, the settings which differ are: The FTE Hours - the default weekly hours, e.g. 37.5 for academic related (May not be applicable if the ‘Link Default Hours to Personnel’ setting is in use)
Base Entitlement – for a full time staff member before any pro rata calculations or long service days, e.g. 38 days or equivalent in hours
The leave year start and end dates – e.g. running 1st Oct-30th Sept
The associated items affecting the entitlement (where applicable) are:
Holiday Schemes
Long Service Schemes
Follow the New Balance Decision Tree to determine when a new Balance is required, and when it can be linked to existing Holiday and Long Service schemes.
Standard University Annual Leave Entitlement
It is expected that most appointments will follow the standard University leave arrangements. I.e. A base entitlement of 38 days’ leave pro rata and a leave year running 1st Oct - 30th Sept.

Long Service Increments
Each increment represents a stage in the long service scheme. The value recorded in the ‘Floating Entitlement’ column is the number of additional days that will automatically awarded at that stage, based on that employee’s length of service. The days are cumulative, so each increment only needs to display the number of additional days awarded at that stage.
By default, the leave is awarded at the start of the leave year during which the employee crosses the threshold (anniversary year). To award the additional leave at the start of the following leave year, you need to increase the months by 12.
In the above example, an employee is entitled to an additional day of leave at the start of the leave year following their 5th anniversary.
The system would not award any additional leave until the start of the leave year during which the employee’s continuous service is scheduled to exceed 72 months (6 years).
Balance calendar

al leave until the start of the leave year during which the employee’s continuous service is scheduled to exceed 72 months (6 years).
Balance calendar Each Balance has its own Balance Calendar, which determines the start and end dates of the leave year (periods), and the rules for carrying forward leave from one leave year to the next.
These must be extended each year to cover the next calendar year. For example, if Annual Leave is managed in yearly blocks the Annual Leave balance calendar defines the start date and end date of each leave year (period) and specifies any carry forward rules. It is not possible to close a balance period (complete a period end) until the next period has been configured on the balance calendar.
You may find it useful to refer to the guides - HOW TO - Update Holiday Schemes v1.1.docx and HOW TO – Maintain calendars in WFM
Balance entitlements
Each Balance needs its own set of Balance Entitlements. The Balance Entitlements determine amount of annual leave that a full-time employee receives to take on dates of their choosing (Personal Leave). In PeopleXD, this is categorised as Floating leave. For every leave year (period) a Balance Entitlement must be set.
Calculating Floating leave days/hours

eopleXD, this is categorised as Floating leave. For every leave year (period) a Balance Entitlement must be set.
Calculating Floating leave days/hours If a Holiday Scheme has been linked to the Balance, the Balance entitlement must offset the number of closure days in the Holiday Scheme. The number of closure dates can vary year on year, so the floating leave values may need to fluctuate to reflect these changes. To determine the number of floating days needed in any specific year, use the following formula:
Floating days + Closure days = Base entitlement
Note: If the Holiday Scheme includes closure day(s) which are awarded on top of the base entitlement, such as discretionary additional leave days awarded by the VC in certain years, and you do not want these days to reduce the amount of Personal Leave the employee has, ensure you either increase the base entitlement value (e.g. to 39) or ignore the leave in the closure days value

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Payroll Calendars for a

Items covered include:

1.2. What is a Payroll Calendar?
A payroll c alendar must be generated for each company within an organisation . The following points
should be noted:
• A payroll calendar must be generated for each company within an organisation.
• The calendar consists of the year broken up into week numbers, e.g. 202001, 202002, 202003
etc.
• The calendar tracks the period end date for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay groups.
The period end date for monthly pay groups will always be the last day of the month.
• The payroll calendar does not track the payment date.
• Period end dates can be offset at a pay group level.
• The calendar will always contain at least the current year and future years.

1. Overview
The ‘Document and Email Generatio n’ feature on CoreHR allows a user to automatically generate
documents / letters / emails based on employee data e.g. employee contracts, letters of offer, hr forms
etc.
This feature is primarily available to users in HR Admin and Recruitment Admin.
Pre-configured templates are created and stored centrally on the system. A user can generate a version
of this document (MS Word or PDF) which may be populated automatically using data held for
employees in HR Admin and applicants & interview panel members in Recruitment. It is possible to
generate an individual document per record, or multiple versions of the same document for multiple
records. Once a document has been generated, there is an option for this to be automatically stored on
the system against an employee’s record, for future reference.
The main users of this feature will be:
 HR Administrator

 Recruitment Administrator

 Manager

The purpose of this guide is to provide guidance on:
 Key concepts & terminology associated with this feature
 How to create and manage templates on CoreHR
 How to generate and review a document or email for one or many records
 How to configure CoreHR to enable the feature for the various users who will require access

1.1. Key Concepts
1.1.1. Document
A ‘document’ refers to a file (MS Word or PDF) that can be generated from CoreHR by merging
employee data into templates that have been stored on the system. These may be used to create
employee contracts, pre-populated HR forms, applicant correspondence etc.
Documents that have been generated on CoreHR may be downloaded by the user to further amend

cts, pre-populated HR forms, applicant correspondence etc.
Documents that have been generated on CoreHR may be downloaded by the user to further amend and print, as required.
Documents may also be automatically stored against an employee’s record on the ir Employee Profile
screen, as part of the document generation.
A user may also upload a document to the Employee Profile, independent of generation process e.g.
uploading a copy of a passport.
1.1.2. Email
System generated emails can be produced and sent automatically from CoreHR to an employee or an
applicant. Emails are typically used to support the recruitment process e.g. to send an invitation for
interview to a candidate. However, these may also be generated to employees within HR Admin.
1.1.3. Template
Templates can be stored on the system to support the production of both documents and emails.
 Document Templates: These are created using MS Word mail merge functionality and uploaded
to CoreHR
 Email Templates: These are created and maintained directly on CoreHR
1.1.4. Template Group
Templates (document or email) may be grouped into various categories e.g. Contracts, Recruitment,
Salary etc. This is an optional grouping and does not need to be used for all or any templates.
1.1.5. Document Type
This is used to group documents that have been generated on the system or uploaded independently

e used for all or any templates.
1.1.5. Document Type
This is used to group documents that have been generated on the system or uploaded independently to an employee’s or applicant’s record. This is an important setting for controlling the visibility of and
access to documents for HR and Recruitment Admins as well as Employees and Managers

1.1.6. Data Source
Standard mail merge functionality employs the use of ‘Data Sources’ which are essentially temporary
files pre-populated with the record data that will become merged into a document or email template.
In this feature, each screen in HR Admin or Recruitmen t Admin from which a document / email can be
generated from, is linked to a specified data source (or data sources). This data source is a set of
employee / applicant / contract / record fields which will be mapped to a template.
Templates are configured, mapped to these fields. When a document or email is generated, a temporary
file (not available to the user) will become populated with data for corresponding record(s). This will
them update the mappings in the generated document / email.

The HR Process Task List functionality has been enhanced in v28 to include a variety of new features.
1. Leaver Task Lists
A new Leaver tab is available on the HR Task List screen, which allows you to define a checklist
of tasks to be completed when an employee is made a leaver on CoreHR e.g. to Assign Leaver
Access.
2. Task Owners
Task list items can now be assigned to a specified owner to complete.
• The task ownership is identified using a specified org role/org group assignment
• For example, access to Assign User Access may be restricted to security administrators
only.
• If a user is not the owner and doesn’t have access to complete a task item, they will
see the item on the Task List screen, which will flag the Org Role responsibl e for
completing the task and they will be prevented from access the task itself.
3. Task List Restrictions
• Task list items can be restricted, allowing you to create tailored task lists for different
employee categories and functions e.g. different task list items to be assigned to
permanent v agency staff.
• This is achieved using criteria groups i.e. only assign this task if the employee is in one

k list items to be assigned to

A new task called Specific UDF is available to be added to all task lists. This allows you to select
a specific UDF that you have set up on People Management for completion as part of the task.
5. Optional Information
The new Optional Information text field is available when configuring every task item. The
information provided here is displayed to the user when completing the task, to give them further
guidance on what they may need to do.
6. All Tasks are Mandatory
In earlier versions, tasks could be flagged as mandatory or optional.
From v28, all tasks are mandatory by default.

i.e. you couldn’t complete task 2 before task 1.

'Failed.'
o Failed: At least one record in the file has failed to migrate into XD.
o Complete: All records in the file have successfully migrated into XD.
• Once Processing is ‘Complete,’ it is no longer possible to review the individual file records. The
records have now been created on XD and are available to view on the corresponding screens.

3. Switch On Employee Onboarding There are two options available when enabling Employee onboarding:
• Enable
Suitable if you are setting up onboarding for the first time on CoreHR OR you do not intend to
import checklists created for pre-v27 Onboarding Checklists on CoreHR.

be completed before Employee onboarding is enabled.

To enable Employee onboarding:

(pre-v27) will be available to users within the Classic UI.

available to new starters will not be there anymore and instead Employee Onboarding will
be made available for employees to complete their tasks i.e. the Social Hub.
• Employee Onboarding is not available in the Classic UI.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality in
People Management and how this is used. This includes:
• What is Employee Onboarding and when it used by employees?
• The difference between ‘new starter onboarding’ and ‘existing employee cross-boarding’.
• An overview of the Social Hub dashboard.
• Detailed guidance on the main elements of the Social Hub dashboard and how they may be
used.
• Tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or hr administrator.
Employee Onboarding is highly configurable to ensure that every organisation can manage the
onboarding and cross-boarding experience based on their own requirements. This document does not
cover configuration guidance. For full training on how to set up and configure each element of Employee
Onboarding, see the Employee Onboarding v28: How to Configure - User Guide.
1.2. What is Employee Onboarding?
Employee Onboarding is a platform that supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-joiners,
while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees. For example:

supports onboarding guidance for new joiners and re-joiners,
while also supporting continuous onboarding guidance for existing employees. For example: • New starter onboarding for employees joining or re-joining the organisation.
• Cross-boarding for existing employees who move to new contracts, appointments, and/or
teams.
• The requirement to release new Checklist Items to existing employees.
• A platform encouraging existing employees to engage with their wider team.
Employees can commence onboarding before the join the organisation i.e. before their sta rt date or
rehire date. If this is the case, the employee will need a CorePortal account (to be created in the same
way as you generally issue CorePortal accounts). However, they will only have access to the Social
Hub until their start date has elapsed. They will not be able to access any other part of the CorePortal
e.g. Employee Dashboard won’t be available to them until they have started.:

Continuous Onboarding
If an existing employee is given a new contract e.g. moving from ‘Department A’ to ‘Department B’:
• Global Checklist Items with no restrictions can be made available to the employee to complete.
• If there are Checklist Items that have been restricted to only be seen by employees within a
‘Department A’ defined Criteria Group, these Checklist Items are no longer relevant, therefore,
are no longer available for the employee to complete.
• If there are Checklist Items that have been restricted to only be seen by employees within a
‘Department B’ defined Criteria Group, these Checklist Items are now relevant, therefore, are
available for the employee to complete.

the hr administrator will still have the ability to update and amend the details for each individual contract
of employment, as required.

prevent an application from being submitted or caution the recruitment administrator as part
of the shortlisting process.

5.8.1. What is a Schedule
A schedule on a vacancy is used to track interview rounds and assessments associated with the vacancy.
For example
• Pre-interview assessments for a group of candidates.
• Multiple rounds of interviews.
For each schedule you need to define key information such as dates, times and locations. Interview panel
members can be assigned to one or all the schedules as required so that they can see the details of who is
to be interviewed and access their application details.
Applicants are assigned to each schedule as they progress through the vacancy process. For example, an
applicant could be assigned to the following schedules:
• Group assessment
• Interview round 1
• Interview round 2

5.8.3. Multi-Day Schedules
What are Multi-Day Interview Schedules?
A multi-day interview schedule is a schedule that is configured to take place over several days.

Day Schedules
What are Multi-Day Interview Schedules?
A multi-day interview schedule is a schedule that is configured to take place over several days. When creating this type of schedule, it is possible to update the following schedule items per day:
• Start Time
• End Time
• Morning Break Time
• Lunch Time
• Evening Break Time
• Board Convenes Time
This ensures that when the system automatically identifies available time slots for a schedule, the times
associated with individual days are taken into consideration.
It is possible to remove an entire date/dates between the defined start and end dates i.e. schedule dates do
not have to run concurrently.
It is also possible to ensure that weekend dates are included OR omitted when defining a multi -day schedule.

The new process replaces the current manual process where People Management Admins are
required to manually calculate entitlements remaining from the previous appointment, complete
adjustments to the new appointment’s entitlement to reflect the remaining carry over, and re-enter
future dated leave/absence records.
The following steps have been automated as part of the transfer of balances:
• The previous appointments balance is pro-rata calculated at date of replacement to
determine entitlement remaining.
• The new appointments balance is assigned and the entitlement remaining from the
previous appointment is applied to the carried forward.
• Narrative is included on the carried forward adjustments to support the transfer.

management, a checklist for fixed-term staff etc. The amount of checklists defined on CoreHR is optional
and based on the organisation’s requirements. It is possible to simply use the existing ‘Default Checklist’
for all employees.

1.2. Allowances in HR vs Payroll
The allowances that are setup in People Management for the employee’s contract are ‘permanent /
reoccurring allowances’. These are allowances that are assigned to the employee’s contract for a fixed
or open-ended period. Every ti me payroll is run for that employee’s contract , the allowance amount is
calculated and included in the employee’s pay.
For example: An employee is assigned a ‘Night Duty’ allowance of £25 per period (e.g. per month). The
allowance was assigned to the empl oyee’s contract with a start date of 1 st March 2019. This is open-
ended i.e. no planned end date exists for the allowances and the intention is that the employee should
continue to receive the allowance until further notice. Every month when Payroll is pro cessed, the
allowance of £25 will be added to the employee’s calculated salary.
Once-off allowance payments are not recorded in People Management. These are once off payment s
that will be made for the employee for the current pay period e.g. a bonus payment. These are captured
directly in Payroll.

1.3. Allowance Types There are a number of types of allowances supported on CoreHR.
Allowance Type Description
Value
These Allowances will pay a single specified amount every pay period e.g. if an
employee is on a monthly pay group and has a standard value allowance of
£100, then £100 will be paid every month.
There are 2 types of ‘Value’ based allowances:
• Standard Value: A specified amount is defined on the Allowance Pay
Code and that set amount is paid for all employees linked to it, for every
pay period e.g. Night Duty allowance is set at £30 per period for
everyone.
• Variable Value : The amount to be paid is specific to the individual
employee. This is not captured at the Pay Code level but it specified
when setting up the allowance for the employee. This allows different
employees to receive varying values for the same Allowance Pay Code
e.g. Mary has a Night Duty allowance of £30 but John has a Night Duty
allowance of £40.
Please note: if an Allowance is required to have a standard value set up at Pay
Code level for the majority of employees, but it is required to capture different
values for that Allowance for a handful of employees, the Pay Code standard
value can be overwritten when it is being set up for each employee. Please refer

These Allowances will pay a percentage of the employee’s actual salary every
pay period
e.g. Tom gets £1000.00 per week gross pay. He gets a shift allowance of 12%
of gross pay , so each week he is in receipt of and additional £120.00 shift
allowance. Like the Standard Value Allowances the shift allowance percentage
can be set up either at a Pay Code or employee level.
Scaled
Allows for a scale of specific allowance rates to be recorded on CoreHR and for
a point on that scale to be assigned to the employee (similar to Pay Scale type

This deducts a specified amount from the employee’s salary every pay period A negative Allowance is used in cases such as maternity pay or social welfare
where the employee keeps a payment from the government a nd needs an
amount deducted from their gross pay which is non-taxable and non-PRSIable.
E.g. Mary is on maternity leave. She receives and keeps the cheque from social

want to give Mary £500 gross which is made up of £266 of maternity pay from
the company and £244 of social welfare maternity pay.
To pay maternity pay correctly in this instance we do the following:
• Allow the system to generate Gross Pay of £500 for Mary
• Set Up a Negative allowance, deduct from the gross amount
• Attach the allowance to Mary with a value of £244 Euro
This will deduct £244 from Mary’s taxable and PRSIable gross pay. A record of
the payment is on the system and can be queried from reporting and the pay
history.

2. Changing / Amending End Dates
2.1. Change End Date for a Leaver
It is possible to amend the end date provided for a leaver in People Management. This is done by
amending the end date for the employees last contract. This will amend their overall End Date.
To change an end date:
1. Search for the employee in the Command Centre > Employee screen.
2. Click the View button for the required employee.
3. In the Summary section, click on the button and select Amend End Date for the relevant
appointment.
4. If the employee has multiple contracts or has had multiple contract amendments, ensure that
the correct contract sequence is identified:
• Appointment Status is Ended / Ending.
• End Date is populated.
5. Select the option Amend End Date.
The Modify Post Appointment End Date screen opens.

2.2. Remove End Date for a Leaver
It is possible to remove the end date provided for a leaver in People Management. This is done by

1.2. What are HR Process Task Lists? Task Lists are used to define a set of steps that must be completed as part of a New Starter, New
Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire or Leaver process.
Once a new contract has been assigned to an employee as part of the new hire, rehire or new contract
steps on People Management, the task list will pop up on screen. This will present the user with a list
of mandatory and optional steps to be completed. The user can then click on a step and be redirected
to the screen required to input the data e.g. if the step is ‘Allowances’, clicking on this will open the ‘Add
Allowances’ screen.
Different task lists can be created for each process type.
The advantage of using the task list feature includes:
• Ability to direct the user to ensure the required employee and contract details are updated.
• One central location is provided to allow the user to jump directly to the required scree ns to
update the data.
• The task list can be closed and reopened as many times as necessary before completion.

1.2.1. What Contracts can be Updated?
This functionality is used to change the start date that has been set up for an employee’s contract. This

For options 1 & 2 above:

a. Contract Start Date
b. Latest Start Date
Changes to additional contracts will not result in any update to the Date First Joined or the Rehire Date.
If the substantive contract is updated, the corresponding Substantive Date is also be updated.
1.2.2. What Contracts Cannot be Updated?
The start date for the following contracts cannot be updated using the Amend Contract Start Date
functionality:
• Replacement Contracts.
• Contracts that have been processed on Payroll.

1.2.1. HR Access
In CoreHR, the hr administrator’s access to employees on the system is restricted based on their
designated HR Access. This HR Access is aligned to an Organisational Unit e.g. this may be set to:
• Company = ABC Solutions
• Department = Human Resources
• Division = Shared Services
Every employee on CoreHR will be assigned to at least one contract. That contract will specify the
Organisation Units that the employee’s position is aligned to e.g.
• Company = ABC Solutions
• Department = Human Resources
• Division = Shared Services
If the user has access to the Department e.g. Human Resources, then they will be able to see the
employee record and their contract in that department.
However, if the user doesn’t have access to the Department e.g. Finance, then they will not be able to
see the employee record and their contract in that department.

them into a new contract within their organisation, then they need to complete a ‘Transfer Request’.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
This guide is used to explain how to use the Payroll Instruction Forms via People Management. In order
to capture and automatically share pay-affecting information with Payroll, as part of the
joiner/mover/leaver processes e.g. holidays to be paid to a leaver, student loans for a new hire etc.
Within this User Guide you will learn how to:
• Create a custom form.
• Add a new HR task list item of Payroll Instructional Form.
• Assign a specific Org Role to this task.
• View & action the task on Pay Portal.
1.2. What is a Payroll Instructional Form?
A Payroll Instructional Form is a method of communication that is sent to Payroll directly from HR in
terms of details that are going to affect the employee’s payroll record once processed. Examples of
these items include:
1. Balance adjustments needed for holidays owed to an employee.
2. Outstanding student loan payments.
3. PAYE / Tax Code changes.
4. Holiday/Average Pay calculations.

3. PAYE / Tax Code changes.
4. Holiday/Average Pay calculations. 5. Hours (i.e. Overtime).
6. Adhoc Payments (i.e. Bonuses & once off payments).
7. Pension changes.
8. Pay Awards inc Position and Point updates/increases via AdHoc module (maybe this is covered
in the Salary approvals piece)
9. Late Leavers / Joiners / Rejoiners
10. Temp Reinstatements
11. Any cancel/manual payments to be processed
12. Cost Allocation changes

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
Note This guide is only applicable if an organisation is managing the assignment of pension schemes for employees at contract level, rather than person level. Please refer to the relevant Payroll
training resources for guidance on managing pension scheme assignments at employee level.
This document provides guidance on how to manage pension schemes for employees by directly
assigning these to their contract records. This includes:
• Linking pension schemes to post profile records.
• Assigning a pension scheme to contracts.
• Amending existing pension scheme assignments.
• How the assignment of a pension scheme is ended.
• The payslip impact of the ‘Pension by Appointment’ option.
This docu ment does not provide guidance on how to manage pensions schemes f or employees at
employee level.
1.2. Pension by Appointment vs Pension by Person
CoreHR provides the facility to capture Pension Scheme assignments for employee at either Person or
Appointment level. An organisation will configure the CoreHR application to manage pensions using
either of these options. Only one option can be enabled at a time. It is not possible to define a
combination of these options
1.2.1. Pension by Person
Pension Schemes are assigned directly to the employee’s record.
• This is managed in Payroll and not in HR.

new contracts etc. will not impact on the pension scheme assignment.
Note If this option is used, the Pension Contributions screen will be read-only. This means that
the screen:
• will display the details of any pension assigned to the person.
• will not provide the ability to update or amend the pension assignments, regardless of the
menu options assigned to the user.

to all or some of these.

2. Overview
2.1. The Purpose of the Document
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the data migration functionality on
People XD and highlight the enhancements made in v28 to support existing and upgrading customers.
This includes:
• What is the data migration tool and when is it used?
• How to complete a data migration.

to support existing and upgrading customers.
This includes:
• What is the data migration tool and when is it used?
• How to complete a data migration. • How to resolve errors during upload.
• How to clear down files (reverse the migration) for uploaded files and processed records.
This document does not provide detailed gui dance on how to complete each of the data migration
templates. Refer to the helper files that can be downloaded from the Data Migration Templates widget.
The Data Migration Update Facility widget is not covered in this document. Please refer to the Data
Migration Update Facility user guide.
2.2. What is the Data Migration Tool?
The data migration process typically occurs when an organisation is initially implementing XD and is
used to bulk import their records.
This includes:
• Employees and their associated personal details.
• Contracts and their associated elements, including salary details.
• Occupational absences and payroll cumulative history.
• Selected reference data elements.
This tool provides a set of 26 data migration templates. These can be downloaded from XD and
populated with actual system records. These files can then be loaded to XD, validated and processed
so that the corresponding records are created on the system.
2.3. Data Migration vs Updates

se files can then be loaded to XD, validated and processed
so that the corresponding records are created on the system.
2.3. Data Migration vs Updates The data migration tool is used to insert new records to XD. This is not used to change / update existing
records. Both the Data Migration Templates and Data Migration Options widgets are used for this
process.
The Data Migration Update Facility widget is used to update existing records. Please refer to the Data
Migration Update Facility user guide.

Migration experience within the Modern UI.

in XD. If yo u are not an Early Adopter then please refer to updates in XD Hub for self -service
configuration of Data Migration improvements.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the new features and
functionality introduced to absence pay in Payroll.
The new features and functionality are applicable to payroll occupational or statutory absence
types, such as:
• Maternity Pay • Paternity Pay
• Adoptive Pay • Shared Parental Pay
This new functionality is applicable doesn’t apply to non-payroll absences, such as:
• Annual Leave
• Privilege Day
• Innovative Thinking Days
• Jury Service Leave
1.2. Overview
The new features and functionality introduced to the absence pay in Payroll include:
1. Employee Absence Information
Several new screens have been added to the Employee Dashboard in Payroll where you can view
employees’ absence information, including:
• The Absence Summary screen, which displays the following tabs:
o Absences Pay Per Period – displays summarised absence pay information relating to
groups of occupational absence days/hours processed. The Absence Display Settings

o WFM Absences Current Period – displays absence days/hours recorded this period in
Workforce Management highlighting which have been processed by Payroll.
o Information Per Absence Type – displays the key absence information for each of the
employee’s absence types and absence rules.
• The Occupational Detail screen is an enhanced version of the Back Office Absence Manager
Maintenance screen, which allows you to:
o To View Historical Occupational Absence details.
o To View Predicted Occupational Absence details.

2. Absence Period Daily Rate
The Absence Period Daily Rate introduces new methods for calculating an employee’s absence
daily rate. The absence daily rate can now be derived by dividing the period salary by the number
of days in the period. Note the following:
• The absence period daily rate calculation method can be configured at the following levels:
o Company Level.
o Pay Group Level.
o Absence Rule Level.
• The number of days in the period can be derived from:
o Calendar Days.
o Monday to Friday Days.
o Workforce Management Work Days.
• Allowance Groups allow you to select non-percentage allowance pay codes to include in
the calculation for deriving the employees’ absence daily rate.
3. Absence Rate Override
The Absence Rate Override screen allows you to override an employee’s daily or hourly rate from
a specified effective date. Note the following:

4. Absence Pay Prediction
The Absence Pay Prediction task is a new overnight task which calculates future occupational
absences based on the WFM absence start and end dates. The Absence Pay Prediction task
predicts the date the occupational pay is expected to drop or increase, based on:
• The absence entitlement rule assigned to the employee.
• The employee’s FTE.
For example, full pay to half pay or half pay to zero pay.
The Absence Pay Predict ion task can be manually run for a single employee via Employee
Dashboard in Payroll.
5. Absence Reversals
If the cancelled absence relates to the previous payroll period, payroll can now reverse the
transactions related to the absence.
There are two reversal solutions available:
• Fully Automatic Reversals: Allows the system to reverse the payment automatically, while
informing you of the reversal via a Payroll Message.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure auto enrolment. This
will include how to set parameters used to control auto enrolment.
1.2. What is Auto Enrolment?
Auto Enrolment is a government initiative and requires every employer of staff normally working
in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions
towards their employee's pension.

f normally working
in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions
towards their employee's pension. Employees will be automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme if they are not
already active members of a workplace pension scheme that meets a set of minimum standards.
The employer must make pension contributions to the pension scheme , and the worker may also
have to contribute. Workers who do not want to join the scheme may opt -out for a three-year
period. But, employers are required to continue automatically enrolling el igible workers who’ve
opted out, every three years.
Eligible employees are workers who:
• Are aged between 22 and State Pension Age;
• Earn over the earnings threshold, and
• Work, or ordinarily work in the UK and have a contract of employment (i.e. so is a worker
and not a self-employed contractor), or who have a contract to provide work and / or
services personally (so can’t sub-contract to a third party).

• Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP)

• Ordinary Statutory Sick Pay (OSSP)
• Adoption Pay (SAP)

1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2021/22
and prepare for the 2022/23 tax year. This document covers the following:
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.

1.2. What is Year End?
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.
• Issue Employees with a P60.

Access Limited Distribution Page 10 of 101 3.2.1. Overview
On 7 September 2021 the government announced a new 1.25% Health and Social Care Levy to
fund investment in the NHS and social care.
The Levy will be effectively introduced from April 2022 when National Insurance Contributions
(NICs) for working age employees, self-employed people and employers will increase by 1.25% and
be added to the existing NHS allocation. This increased NIC rate is automatically applied from April
2022 within the payroll system.
From April 2023, the Levy will be formally separated from NICs and also apply to the earnings of
individuals working above State Pension age and National Insurance Contribution rates will return
to 2021-22 levels. A software update for this will be part of next year’s UK Year end update.
To ensure taxpayers understand that their increased contribution is helping fund public services,
HMRC are asking employers to put a message on payslip templates explaining what these funds
will be used for. The message applies to all payslips for the Tax year 2022/23 and should read
“1.25% uplift in NICs funds NHS, health & social care”.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2022/23
and prepare for the 2023/24 tax year. This document covers the following:
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release.

• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task.
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2023/24 tax year.
1.2. What is Year End?
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.
• Issue Employees with a P60.

6.5.2. Employment Allowance
The Employment Allowance (EA) allows businesses and charities to reduce their Employer's Class
1 NIC liability by up to £5,000 per tax year.
The EA is only available to businesses and charities with an Employer's Class 1 NIC liability of below
£100,000 in the preceding tax year.
The EA is considered a form of de minimis state aid. There is a ceiling on how much state aid any
Organisation can receive under the de minimis rules. For most businesses, this ceiling will be
€200,000 over a three -year rolling period (different levels apply to agriculture, fisheries, road
transport, and industrial sectors).
Note:
If claiming the EA, it is your responsibility to check:
• Your Secondary Class 1 NICs liability for the previous tax year was less than £100,000.
• You have space to accommodate the full £5,000 within your relevant three-year ceiling,
regardless of how much EA you claim each year , if you receive any other form of de
minimis state aid.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of this Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to process the Year End for 2022/23
and prepare for the 2023/24 tax year. This document covers the following:
• The legislative rate changes as outlined in the Budget.
• The software changes introduced as part of the UK Year End Software Release.
• The tasks to complete before your Year End Cleardown task.
• The tasks to complete after your Year End Cleardown task.
• The steps required to configure your Payroll System correctly for the 2023/24 tax year.
1.2. What is Year End?
At the end of the tax year, after the final Payrolls have been processed, you are required to:
• Submit a Final EPS to HMRC.
• Complete the Pre Year End Checks.
• Run the Year End Cleardown task.
• Complete your Post Year End Tasks.
• Issue Employees with a P60.
The Year End Cleardown task in Payroll completes the following tasks:

table.
• Generates the Payroll Company Calendar for the next two years.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide detailed guidance on the ‘Wage Warnings’ feature
on PeopleXD, including:
• Where the wage warning validation is applied.
• How the warning validation is calculated.
• How to configure ‘Minimum Wage’, ‘Living Wage’ & ‘Apprentice Wage’ rates on

Wage’ / ‘Apprentice Wage’ rates on PeopleXD.
1.2. How do the Wage Warnings Work?
1.2.1. What are Wage Warnings?
PeopleXD provides an option to validate the rate entered for an employee’s salary, against
minimum, living and / or apprentice wage rates. This is to inform the user if the salary they
are providing for the employee’s contract is too low.
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on PeopleXD (see

ary they
are providing for the employee’s contract is too low.
Rates for minimum wage, living wages and apprentice wages can be setup on PeopleXD (see 2. Configuring the Rates). These can be added to on an annual basis, as new rates are
released for each new tax year.
PeopleXD will calculate if the salary supplied for an employee’s contract meets the minimum
/ living / apprentice wage rates based on:
• The rates defined on PeopleXD and their effective date.
• The employee’s date of birth.
• Contracted hours and weeks (or FTE Weeks per Year).
People Management: Wage Warnings – Configuration Guide

• For apprentice rates, validation is applied to confirm that the employee / contract is
apprentice.
• Where multiple countries are setup, the appropriate rates for the employee’s Pay
Group country.
Minimum wage & apprentice rates are not mutually exclusive. The system will first check to
see if the employee’s contract is an apprentice type contract.
• If it is - apprentice rates are used in validation.
• If it isn’t - minimum wage rates are used in validation
1.2.2. Where is Wage Warning Validation Available?

3.1. Validation Steps
The same validation checks are made when a salary is awarded on any of these screens:
• New hire / rehire wizards

The system will first check if the following details have been supplied for the contract:
1. Date of Birth (Required to determine employee’s age)
2. Contracted Hours
3. Contracted Weeks
If blank, the system will default to use the value in the FTE Weeks per Year parameter

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how the Payscale Restriction Matrix may
be used on CoreHR to provide an additional element of control to the step of awarding a Pay Scale

guidance on how the Payscale Restriction Matrix may
be used on CoreHR to provide an additional element of control to the step of awarding a Pay Scale to an employee. This includes:
• An overview of the Payscale Restriction Matrix feature.
• How to configure matrix rules.
• How to enable or disable the restriction.
1.2. What is the ‘Payscale Restriction Matrix’?
It is possible to restrict the list of Pay Scales that are available to a user to select for an employee’s
salary, based on certain em ployee or contract attributes. A matrix of rules can be configured on
CoreHR to identify the Pay Scales that are applicable to specific employee attributes e.g. Country,
Division, Employment Status etc.
When a hr administrator is creating the salary for an employee, the system will check to see if the
record meets any of the rules defined on the matrix and will only display the Pay Scales that match
those rules.
For example, if the Pay Scales “Grade 1” and “Grade 2” should only apply to UK based employees,
then the hr administrator will only see those Pay Scales when the employee’s address is based in
Country of UK.
Care needs to be taken when defining the matrix of rules to ensure that all employee scenarios
are catered for because if an employee does not match any rule, no Pay Scale will be available.

3.1. Parameter to Enable the Restriction
The restriction is parameter controlled. This means that once the matrix of rules has been defined,
the restriction must be switched on, to ensure the Pay Scale lists are restricted for the end users.
To enable the restriction:
1. Quick jump to the Site Manager widget and Open Admin Settings.
2. Search for the parameter = “cp_rest_pay_scale_matrix”
3. Update the parameter;
a. Y = Restriction is enabled
b. N = Restriction is not enabled
4. Click Save to save changes

shortlisting process i.e.

4.1. Assessment Scorecards Overview
The Assessment Scorecard feature allows individual interview panel members to submit unique assessment details per applicant across the various stages of the recruitment process. Shortlisting
Assessment Scorecards can be created and linked to the Interview Panel widget. Each individual panel
member can submit their own unique scorecard for each applicant that they are reviewing during
the shortlisting process.
Interview schedule Assessment Scorecards can also be created and associated with each
individual interv iew schedule. Each individual panel member can submit their own unique
scorecard for each applicant for each round of interviews that they are assigned to.
For both the shortlisting and interview schedule Assessment Scorecards , the recruitment
administrator has the option to view the total averaged assessment score, for each round, per
applicant.
It is possible to add an Assessment Scorecard for inclusion in the interview panel shortlisting process
i.e. providing panel members with an Assessment Scorecard to complete for each applicant. Repeat
the steps outlined for each individual interview schedule as required. Use the Applicant Status value
to link the scorecard to an interview schedule with the same status i.e. the Status Of value on the

1.2. What are iCues?
iCues are intelligent trigger -based reports, designed to proactively send alerts to stakeholders,
when certain thresholds are breached/events are occurring.
Examples of how iCues could be used include:
• Alert a manager when one of their employees is approaching the sick leave threshold.
• Alert a manager of overlapping leave.
• Alert an HRD when attrition rates spike.
• Alert the FD when costs are increasing.
• Alert an employee when they have a large annual leave balance remaining.
• Alert an employee/manager of an important date e.g. anniversary, birthday etc.
The foundation for an iCue is an intelligent report built in CoreInsight or downloaded from the
Report Store, which is used to trigger a notification to a specified recipient.
• The report includes complex calculations that are used to determine when these
thresholds are breached, or events are about to occur.
• CoreHR runs the iCue report on a specified frequency (daily/weekly/monthly).

1.2. What is Insight?
Insight is an in-application reporting tool to help employees and managers gain perspective on their business operations. It encompasses the process of transforming your People XD
data into reportable datasets and visualising that data into reports, graphs and tables that
expose valuable insights.
XD Insight is about visualising, understanding, and acting on data and provides users with
the following features:
• A reporting homepage to view recent reports that you have created, view reports
that have been shared with you, have a full searchable l ist of all reports you have
access to, Users can view, edit, and clone reports with the ability to launch the Create
Report Wizard.
• Users can create standard listing reports or cross tab reports. A report can be created
from the various areas that are available to the user. E.g. Recruitment, Payroll, etc.
The user can then select the fields they want as part of that report from the
designated views within that area. If applicable, a user can edit, print, or export the
report to excel.

helps organisations retain high performers.

1. Overview
1.1. Purpose of the Guide
The purpose of this guide is to outline the steps needed to create and set up 360 reviews on the
talent dashboard to be assigned to employees and managers for feedback.
1.2. What are 360 Reviews?
360 reviews are feedback opportunities that enable a group of colleagues to provide feedback on
an employee’s performance and facilitate continuous evaluation. Talent management
administrators can create 360 review questionnaires and assign these either to all employees
across the organisation or to employees that belong to a specific organisational group, e.g. all
employees in Division A. Employees can select from a list of the colleag ues, within their defined
organisational group, and request that they provide feedback for them, using the assigned 360
review form.
The feedback is generally asked for by the manager to whom the employee reports into.
