Naming standards for prompts
In order to maintain a consistent look and feel across the HR Reporting catalogue, parameter prompts must follow certain naming standards. These are outlined below.
The prompt for a person reference must always be Personnel number.
The word “description” is always omitted from prompt text; e.g. if the parameter is for “department description”, the prompt must be simply Department.
Prompts of more than one word should only capitalise the first word; e.g. a prompt for the “employee status” value should be Employee status, not “Employee Status”.

Appendix: Free-text multi-value parameters
Many reports have free-text parameters which will accept multiple values in a comma-separated list, e.g. a list of pay codes. This enables report users to type in a list of the exact codes they want to see in the report, without having to scroll through a long drop-down LOV to select each code.
The SQL which supports a free-text multi-value parameter is a little complicated, so here’s a worked example for the pay code parameter shown above.
The WITH clause
Free-text multi-value parameters rely on something called a “WITH” clause, which is a bit of SQL which defines a temporary dataset whose output is available to be referenced in subsequent queries.

(WITH temporary_dataset AS (SELECT :Parameter AS temporary_item FROM DUAL)
SELECT
…rest of SELECT statement… )
Example:

SELECT
PABI_PAY_HISTORY.PAYROLL_PERIOD as PAYROLL_PERIOD… )
The WITH clause here has created a temporary view called paycodetext which contains a temporary item called paycode_text. The values available for the paycodetext.paycode_text item are defined by whatever the report user enters in the :PayCode parameter free-text field.

Context This document outlines the release and deployment processes for reports in the HR Reporting catalogue. These processes were designed to support robust version control of all the report suites which comprise the HR Reporting catalogue, to ensure that:
users have access only to the most recent version of any report suite
there is only a single “active” version of any given report suite at any given time
previous versions of amended or retired report suites (where applicable) are available in case they need to be viewed or restored to active use
NB: The most important aspect of version control for the HR Reporting catalogue is this: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level.
This means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite.

his means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite. For example, say you are making a change to the report suite PERDEP01 Staff in Post. This report suite consists of 13 separate .RDL files. Even if you are only making a change to one of those 13 .RDLs, you must update the version number on all 13 .RDLs – that is, if you update e.g. the Full Data Set.RDL and promote it from Version 6.0 to Version 7.0, you must also promote the version numbers for the rest of the .RDL files within the report suite to the new version number.

What if you haven’t actually changed every .RDL file?
Generally speaking, when you update a report suite that contains multiple .RDL files, you will only be changing the SQL code in a few of those .RDLs, not all of them. If you’ve got some .RDL files in your report suite which have not been edited, use this Report Summary Header instead – it’ll make it obvious to anyone who opens the file that the code for this particular .RDL wasn’t updated when the report suite version changed:

Most importantly, users can also search for the Change ID on OSM and find the full details of and justification for the update – this is a major time-saver when reviewing SQL queries!
Note that for new reports, you will still need to include these details in the Report Summary header. The version will be “1.0” and the change request should detail both the function of the new report and the justification for creating it.

Live Reports Tracker The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet which contains details of all active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, including each report’s name, where it is filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, and which AD groups it is shared with.

The report’s prefix (e.g. PERDEP01)
The report’s name (e.g. Staff in Post)
The report’s location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy (e.g. Home > Personnel > Current Reports)
The AD groups which have permission to view the report in the HR Reporting_LIVE environment (e.g. HRIS-RR-PERDREP – Personnel).

A data source is technically the source of the data which is returned by a report query, i.e. the PeopleXD database which powers your reports (UOXC, UOXP, etc.). In Visual Studio, though, the term “data source” refers to something more like a connection profile – it’s where you both define which PeopleXD database you’re going to use, and provide the login credentials for accessing that database.

ction profile – it’s where you both define which PeopleXD database you’re going to use, and provide the login credentials for accessing that database. There are two shared data sources held in all of the HR Reporting Visual Studio solutions and used across the majority of reports:
Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount: This data source is linked to a PeopleXD service account rather than a standard user account. It is primarily used to run the SQL queries for the shared datasets which populate report parameters, e.g. to retrieve all department codes for use in a parameter’s drop-down list.

Context
Shared datasets are SQL queries which are available to re-use across multiple report (.RDL) files. In HR Reporting, shared datasets are used to retrieve reference data from PeopleXD, in order to populate drop-down lists for report parameters.
Example: Many reports have a “Department” parameter, which allows users to specify which department(s) they want to see returned in the report results. It looks like this:
The shared dataset LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is the source of information for the “Department” parameter’s drop-down list. The shared dataset queries PeopleXD’s database and returns a list of all active departments. This list is then attached to the “Department” parameter, so that users can select the departments in which they are interested.
Because LOV_Optional_Department.rsd is a shared dataset, it can be attached to any report which has a “Department” parameter.
Shared datasets are managed in two places: Visual Studio, where they are created and amended, and the HR Reporting environments, where they are deployed to run alongside reports. See below for detailed guidance.

A note on naming conventions All shared datasets are prefixed with the phrase “LOV_Optional”, because shared datasets return lists of values (LOVs) from which users can select the options in which they are interested. Shared datasets must adhere to the following naming conventions to make it easy to identify what sort of data a given dataset might return.
If the dataset returns reference codes, the convention is:
LOV_Optional + Reference item_Code
If the dataset returns reference descriptions, the convention is:
LOV_Optional_Reference item
If the dataset returns reference codes and descriptions, the convention is:
LOV_Optional + Reference item +_and_Description

The Shared Dataset Properties window will open.
All shared datasets have the following properties:
Name – the name of the dataset .RSD file (this must follow the naming conventions outlined above).
Data source – the shared data source for the dataset. This should always be Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount.

A shared dataset (.RSD) is like a report (.RDL): both run SQL code which queries the PeopleXD database to retrieve information. Just like reports, shared datasets need to be deployed from Visual Studio to the HR Reporting environments so that users can run the queries.

If a shared dataset does not exist in an HR Reporting environment, it won’t be able to populate drop-down lists for any report parameters which depend on that dataset.
For example, if a report has a parameter for “Department Code”, the shared dataset which retrieves the list of department codes from PeopleXD must exist in the HR Reporting environment, or the parameter will not work.

Editing a shared dataset
Generally speaking, you shouldn’t need to make changes to shared datasets, because they are set up to return data from reference tables within the database – this means that any changes made in the database should automatically be reflected in the shared dataset.
Example: The LOV_Optional_Department dataset is programmed to return a list of all department names from PeopleXD. Whenever a new department is added to PeopleXD, it automatically appears in the shared dataset – you don’t need to do anything to make this happen.
Some shared datasets, however, have hard-coded values or filtered results which may need occasional tweaking.

Some shared datasets, however, have hard-coded values or filtered results which may need occasional tweaking. Example: The LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason dataset is programmed to return a list of absence-related appointment reasons from PeopleXD. The SQL query for this dataset specifies that only appointment reasons which meet certain conditions should be returned, e.g. when the reason includes the term ‘ADOPTION’ or ‘SICKNESS’. If a new absence-related appointment reason is added to PeopleXD, you will need to hard-code it into the shared dataset!

Getting Started with SQL Developer Before you can create or edit reports, you will need to launch the Oracle SQL Developer application and connect to the PeopleXD database you wish to query.
SQL Developer is a remote desktop application. You can find it in your Start menu under “CONNECT Remote Services (RADC)”:
Double-click the entry in your Start menu to launch SQL Developer, and enter your CONNECT login details when prompted – these are necessary in order to access the CONNECT Remote Desktop:

You’ll land on the Welcome Page, which contains links to any databases to which you have previously connected, as well as links to Oracle resources for SQL Developer users. The only thing you’ll generally use here is the Database Connection pane:

If you’ve never used SQL Developer before, you will need to create the database connections you require. This is done by setting up something called a connection profile. See below for details.

Using SQL Worksheets
In order to run reports in SQL Developer, you need to use a worksheet. A worksheet is a page where you write (or copy-paste) the SQL code that you’ll use to query the PeopleXD database. When you launch SQL Developer and connect to a database, SQL Developer opens a worksheet for you automatically in a new tab:

ry the PeopleXD database. When you launch SQL Developer and connect to a database, SQL Developer opens a worksheet for you automatically in a new tab: If you’re building a new report (or simply running a small query of some kind), you can simply type your SQL code into the worksheet. If you’ve got the SQL code for an existing report, you can paste it into the worksheet.
Once you’ve got your code in place, click the little green arrow at the top of the worksheet to execute the code:
SQL Developer will read the code you’ve entered in the worksheet and will query the PeopleXD database for the information you’ve requested. This may take some time, depending on how complicated the query is, so you might see this progress bar whilst SQL Developer works:
Once SQL Developer has finished executing the code, the results of the query will be displayed in the Query Result pane at the bottom of the screen.
Exporting the results
You may wish to export the results of your SQL query to an Excel file for further analysis. To do this, right-click anywhere in the Query Results pane and select “Export…” from the pop-up menu:

You need to specify what file format you wish to export the results to, and where on the network you want the export to be saved. In the “Format” field, select “csv”, and in the “File” field, enter the file-path for the network location to which you are exporting the results:
Note: Never export results to the Desktop or C:\ drive.
SQL Developer is a remote desktop application – you would be exporting results to the remote desktop, not to your own PC! This is a security risk. It also makes it very difficult to access the file once it’s finished exporting!

It also provides a running count of how many rows of data have been exported, which may enable you to estimate when the export should be finished (e.g. if you know there are approximately 1,000 rows of data and the Task Progress pane shows that 500 rows have been exported in 30 seconds, you can safely assume that the remaining 500 rows will be exported in the next 30 seconds).

Tables are datasets organised by columns and rows. The columns are the “attributes” of the table – things like PERSON_REFERENCE and SURNAME. The rows are where the “records” are stored.

ORA-00932: inconsistent datatypes: expected DATE got NUMBER This error occurs if your SQL query is attempting to compare two dates within a calculation or a WHERE condition, and one of the dates is not in “Date” format.
Check for any TRUNC() functions wrapped around dates. The TRUNC() function attempts to read anything within the brackets as if it is in date format. If you feed a non-date variable into a TRUNC() function, such as a text string or an integer, TRUNC() can’t understand what you’re asking it to do.

A solution is effectively a “bucket” in which related files can be stored – there’s a lot more to this concept, but the important thing to remember is that each solution has its own data sources, datasets, and report files.

Context This document outlines the release and deployment processes for reports in the HR Reporting catalogue. These processes were designed to support robust version control of all the report suites which comprise the HR Reporting catalogue, to ensure that:
users have access only to the most recent version of any report suite
there is only a single “active” version of any given report suite at any given time
previous versions of amended or retired report suites (where applicable) are available in case they need to be viewed or restored to active use
NB: The most important aspect of version control for the HR Reporting catalogue is this: versioning is done at the report suite-level, not the .RDL level.
This means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite.

his means that if you update any .RDL files within a report suite, you must update the version number for all the .RDL files within that report suite. For example, say you are making a change to the report suite PERDEP01 Staff in Post. This report suite consists of 13 separate .RDL files. Even if you are only making a change to one of those 13 .RDLs, you must update the version number on all 13 .RDLs – that is, if you update e.g. the Full Data Set.RDL and promote it from Version 6.0 to Version 7.0, you must also promote the version numbers for the rest of the .RDL files within the report suite to the new version number.

By updating the version numbers for each .RDL within a report suite, you ensure that the entire report suite is promoted from one version to the next. This prevents complications like having Full Data Set (Version 6.0) in the same report as Limited Data Set (Version 2.0).

Report Summary headers
The SQL query for every .RDL file contains a “Report Summary” header. This header identifies the following attributes of the .RDL file:
Attribute
Meaning
Name
The name of the report suite
Tab name
The name of the individual .RDL file
Version
The major version of the report suite to which this SQL query belongs
Last updated
Month and year of most recent update to report suite
Change ID
OSM Change Request number
NB

A completed example is shown here:
/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: Appointment Changes
** Version: 5.0
** Last updated: JULY 2021

RT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes
** Tab name: Appointment Changes
** Version: 5.0
** Last updated: JULY 2021 ** Change ID: 20012493
***************************************************/
Whenever you update the version number of a report suite, you must update the Report Summary header for every .RDL file within that report suite to reflect the new version number, the month & year the report suite was updated, and the OSM Change Request number relating to the update.
What if you haven’t actually changed every .RDL file?
Generally speaking, when you update a report suite that contains multiple .RDL files, you will only be changing the SQL code in a few of those .RDLs, not all of them. If you’ve got some .RDL files in your report suite which have not been edited, use this Report Summary Header instead – it’ll make it obvious to anyone who opens the file that the code for this particular .RDL wasn’t updated when the report suite version changed:
/*************** REPORT SUMMARY *******************
** Name: PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes

** Version: 5.0

***************************************************/

***************************************************/ Providing these details in the Report Summary header enables any user reviewing the SQL query to quickly determine which version of the query they are looking at and when it was last updated. Most importantly, users can also search for the Change ID on OSM and find the full details of and justification for the update – this is a major time-saver when reviewing SQL queries!
Note that for new reports, you will still need to include these details in the Report Summary header. The version will be “1.0” and the change request should detail both the function of the new report and the justification for creating it.

There are four HR Reporting solutions (.sln files) in Visual Studio: DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE. The DEV solution is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST solution is mainly restricted to project testing and testing updated reports against specific data in test environments. Version control in Visual Studio is managed in the HR Reporting_QA.sln and the HR Reporting_LIVE.sln.

The DEV environment is used for creating and testing brand-new reports, while the TEST environment is mainly restricted to project testing. Version control is managed in the HR Reporting QA environment and the HR Reporting LIVE environment.

Live Reports Tracker The Live Reports Tracker is a spreadsheet which contains details of all active reports in the HR Reporting catalogue, including each report’s name, where it is filed in the HR Reporting folder hierarchy, and which AD groups it is shared with.
Version control is not managed as such in the Live Reports Tracker, however this document must be updated whenever you create a new report, retire an existing report, or amend any of the following aspects of an existing report:
The report’s prefix (e.g. PERDEP01)
The report’s name (e.g. Staff in Post)
The report’s location within the HR Reporting folder hierarchy (e.g. Home > Personnel > Current Reports)
The AD groups which have permission to view the report in the HR Reporting_LIVE environment (e.g. HRIS-RR-PERDREP – Personnel).
Refer to the process below for further information on when and how to update the Live Reports Tracker.

Creating new report folders
Before you can file the .RDLs for your new report, you’ll need to ensure you’ve actually got a report folder in place for them. Follow this process to create a new report folder in any HR Reporting environment.
Please ensure that you are fully familiar with the use of folder access permissions within HR Reporting before you create a new folder. This is essential in order to avoid data breaches.
Where should your new report folder go?

Format switch(\*)
The Format field switch (\*) defines how to display field results. The format instructions determine the following:
The use of uppercase and lowercase letters
Number formats — for example, whether 9 is displayed as ix (roman numerals) or ninth (ordinal text)

Format switches also retain a field result's formatting when the field is updated.

Numeric format switch (\#)
The Numeric format switch (\#) specifies the display of a numeric result.
For example, the switch \# $#,##0.00 in { = SUM(ABOVE) \# $#,##0.00 } displays a result such as "$4,455.70." If the result of a field is not a number, this switch has no effect.
Note: Quotation marks are not required around simple numeric formats that do not include spaces — for example, { MarchSales \# $#,##0.00 }. For more complex numeric formats and those that include text or spaces, enclose the numeric format in quotation marks, as shown in the following examples. Word adds quotation marks to numeric format switches if you insert a field by using the Field dialog box or the Formula command in the Data group of the Layout tab (Table Tools contextual tab).

Back to formatting switches
Date-Time format switch (\@)
The Date-Time format switch (\@) specifies the display of a date or time. For example, the switch \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" in the field { DATE \@ "dddd, MMMM d, yyyy" } displays "Friday, November 23, 2007." Combine the following date and time instructions — day (d), month (M), and year (y); hours (h) and minutes (m) — to build a date-time format. You can also include text, punctuation, and spaces.
Date instructions:
Month (M)
The letter M must be uppercase to distinguish months from minutes.
M    This format item displays the month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 7.
MM    This format item displays the month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit months. For example, July is 07.
MMM    This format item displays the month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, July is Jul.
MMMM    This format item displays the month as its full name.
Day (d)
The letter d displays the day of the month or the day of the week. The letter d can be either uppercase or lowercase.
d    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 6.

the day of the week or month as a number without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 6. dd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a number with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit days. For example, the sixth day of the month is displayed as 06.
ddd    This format item displays the day of the week or month as a three-letter abbreviation. For example, Tuesday is displayed as Tue.
dddd    This format item displays the day of the week as its full name.
Year (y)
The letter y displays the year as two or four digits. The letter y can be either uppercase or lowercase.
yy    This format item displays the year as two digits with a leading 0 (zero) for years 01 through 09. For example, 1999 is displayed as 99, and 2006 is displayed as 06.
yyyy    This format item displays the year as four digits.
Time instructions:
Hours (h)
A lowercase h bases time on the 12-hour clock. An uppercase H bases time on the 24-hour, or military, clock; for example, 5 P.M. is displayed as 17.
h or H    This format item displays the hour without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 9.
hh or HH    This format item displays the hour with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 09.
Minutes (m)

This format item displays the hour with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit hours. For example, the hour of 9 A.M. is displayed as 09.
Minutes (m) The letter m must be lowercase to distinguish minutes from months.
m    This format item displays minutes without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "m" } displays 2.
mm    This format item displays minutes with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit minutes. For example, { TIME \@ "mm" } displays 02.
Seconds (s)
s    This format item displays seconds without a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds. For example { TIME \@ “s” displays 5.
ss    This format item displays seconds with a leading 0 (zero) for single-digit seconds For example { TIME \@ “ss” displays 05.
A.M. and P.M. (AM/PM)
This displays A.M. and P.M. To change the A.M. and P.M. symbols for Microsoft Windows, change the regional settings in Control Panel.
am/pm or AM/PM    This format item displays A.M. and P.M. as uppercase. For example, { TIME \@ "h AM/PM" } and { TIME \@ "h am/pm" } display 9 AM or 5 PM.

In April 2021, we discovered that some users were unable to run reports on the HR Reporting servers unless they took the steps outlined below – see OSM Problem Record #40002259 for full details.
These steps may prove useful for other browser-related issues.
If a user is experiencing problems with a browser-based process, e.g. running reports or doing work in the Portal, there are some common troubleshooting techniques you can employ to try to resolve the issue. This document explains how to: run an incognito browsing session, clear browsing history, and disable extensions on all common PC browsers.
Incognito browsing
If a user is having problems with a process and you suspect their browser may be to blame, it is useful to try running the process in an “incognito” browser session before you clear their history or disable their extensions.

may be to blame, it is useful to try running the process in an “incognito” browser session before you clear their history or disable their extensions. An incognito session is a temporary browser session that is isolated from the browser's main session and user data – that is, it is “unaware of” any of the cached data or extensions that are normally present when the browser is running.
To open an incognito browser session in any browser, follow the instructions below.
Browser
Directions
Google Chrome
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New incognito window”
Mozilla Firefox
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “New Private Window”
Microsoft Edge
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + N
From the menu: Select “New InPrivate window”
Microsoft Internet Explorer
Keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + P
From the menu: Select “Safety” and then “InPrivate browsing”
The browser session may open in a new tab or a new window, depending on the browser you are using.
If your user is able to run their process successfully in an incognito browsing session, that indicates that you will need to clear their browser history and disable their extensions to allow the user to run their process in a normal browser session. Overview
The Shift Type configuration screen is available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard.
The following menu profile should be assigned in order to gain access to the steps below.
WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES
A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work. Departmental HR Administrators assign the appropriate shift types to appointments via People Management > Work Schedule, but can only assign shift types that have been created by HR Systems.
Shift Types and Daily Work Patterns
Shift Types are formed by assigning a work pattern to each day of the week. A work pattern is the number of hours worked in a day, the start and end times are irrelevant, so an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM.

ee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 08:00AM would require the same work pattern as an employee working 5 hours on a Monday starting at 11:00AM. Work patterns are broken into 3 minute intervals (the lowest number that can be accurately decimalised). The largest work pattern available is a 13 hour day.
On days when employees are not required to work the ‘REST’ work pattern is used.
Rotating/flexible shift patterns
Most employees follow the same pattern each week. If an employee varies between different patterns each week see part B.
If an employee has a flexi-time arrangement, where there is no predefined pattern, they should be assigned one of the standard shifts based on their average daily hours. For example, if someone works 25 hours across 5 days, they should be assigned a shift type with a 5 hour work pattern on each day, Monday-Friday.
Departmental HR should request a new shift type via OSM service request and provide a copy of the Shift Code Generator for the shift type required.
Generating a shift type code
Each shift type has a unique code and a name (description). The codes for weekly shift patterns are generated using the Shift Type Code Generator, with each code represents a unique combination of daily work patterns. This prevents multiple shift types being created with the same pattern. Codes for Rotating shift types are linked to the employee appointments.

e 'Start Day' configured for the Company. For example, if the start day of the Company is Monday then the start date of the calendar must be a Monday. Overview
The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level.
Currently the only override setting being utilised is the Holiday Scheme. The Holiday Scheme calculates when an employee is allowed to book leave and this is derived from the workgroup as default. In certain circumstances where multiple employees share the same workgroup, but have differing holiday terms, then the Holiday Scheme against the workgroup can be overridden at employee level and these are the steps covered in this guide.
NB: To complete this process the following menu options must be enabled:
‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Work Group Override’
‘WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Add/Update Work Group Override’.

Login to PeopleXD
Navigate to the WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Person Maintenance

1.12 Holiday Schemes
During Discovery it was highlighted that the different Departments within the University have different Public Holidays and Company Closure Days.
To ensure that employees are treated to these days off, the dates of the Public Holidays and Company Closure Days have been configured into the Holiday Schemes.
The hours relative to these have been deducted from the employee’s entitlement, leaving just the days left to take at their leisure.
There are three different Holiday Schemes for the different Departments and will only apply to those Departments where employees have been granted a Balance with Entitlements.
By adding the Holiday Scheme to the Annual Leave Balance, the system computes the Annual Leave Balance as follows:

ranted a Balance with Entitlements.
By adding the Holiday Scheme to the Annual Leave Balance, the system computes the Annual Leave Balance as follows: Balance Entitlement from Annual Leave Scheme + Public Holidays/Company Closure Days – any days taken = Remaining Entitlement.
The Holiday Scheme dates have been configured in accordance with those provided in the IG. However, this area of the system will require ongoing maintenance for future years for both the Company Closure Days and the Public Holidays.

Functionality has been enabled to allow Timesheets that have been submitted within a specific time frame that remain unconfirmed at the point of generating timesheets into pay to be allowed to roll over to the next month.

The system uses the ‘Countback’ weeks to determine how many months these hours can be rolled forward for and once exhausted will not include the hours in any roll forward periods.

3.4 Generate Timesheet – inc. Ignore Unconfirmed Hours The Generate Timesheet Process is the process from transferring Online Timesheet Claims from CoreTime to CorePay using a specific set of dates laid out within the User Defined Calendar.
There are two modes of generation – Test and Live explained below
3.4.1 Generate Timesheet – Test Mode
When generating the Timesheet in TEST Mode, the system will automatically draw in all Online Timesheet Claims for the open month within the User Defined Calendar.
In Test Mode, the Generate Timesheet process can be run as many times as required, and for all combinations of Work Groups:
Single Work Group
Selection of Work Groups
All Work Groups.

Navigation: CoreTime Roster > Period End > Generate Timesheets
3.4.2 Generate Timesheet – LIVE Mode
The Timesheets should never be generated in LIVE mode until the very last run and all checks have taken place ready for payment.
When the Timesheets are run in Live Mode, the system will:
Generate the Timesheets for Payment and transfer into CorePay
Update the User Defined Calendar to the next process period

Live Mode, the system will:

Once the Generate Timesheet process has been run in Live, there is not an option to reverse back to the previous month.

Background
A Holiday Scheme is a list of closure dates, such as public/bank holidays and departmental fixed closure days. These dates will be treated as non-working days for anyone linked to the Holiday Scheme (via their Balance). The system using employee work schedules to determine if the employee would normally work on the closure day and adjusts their entitlement accordingly.
A Holiday scheme can be linked to a Balance, but this is optional and Balances will function without a Holiday Scheme. Holiday Schemes should not be used with Accrual Balances.

Different FTE Hours
Different Long Service Schemes
Different leave years
Different Base Entitlement
All Balances linked to a Holiday Scheme must share the same:

What are Work Patterns Work Patterns define a daily work schedule. They identify the different work durations that exist within the organisation and capture the expected working hours for an employee. Selected work patterns are then used to configure an employee’s shift type. Work patterns are an integral part of the system linking to multiple areas.
Accessing the Work Patterns screen
The Work Pattern screen is where administrators can manage work patterns for their organisation. The screen lists all Work Patterns created and shows if they are active or not. This screen can be used to create new work patterns, copy existing work patterns and further configure patterns to organisational requirements.
To access the Work Patterns screen, navigate via
WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > select Work Patterns.
The following Work Patterns screen displays.
There is a search and filter option available on the Work Patterns screen, allowing you to search for a specific work pattern or filter by Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Active or Label.
The screen contains the following fields:

Calculation Method

Active Indicator
When the active indicator is enabled the work pattern is available to be added to a Shift Type.
How to Add a new Work Pattern
To add a new work pattern, complete the following steps:
1. Click Add at the top of the screen.
2. Fill in the mandatory fields Pattern Code, Description, Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Default Hours, Default Start Time, Default End Time, Earliest Start Time.
3. Click OK.
4. Your new Work Pattern will open for you to further configure, using the tabs on the left-hand side. For example, add Standard Hours and Breaks.
5. Once your Work Pattern is fully configured, click Save.
6. Your Work Pattern is now ready to be added to a Shift Type.

How to Copy a Work Pattern
To copy a work pattern, complete the following steps: 1. Select Copy from the 3-dot menu of the work pattern you wish to copy.
2. Fill in the Pattern Code.
3. Fill in the Description.
4. Click OK.
5. Your copied Work Pattern will open for you to further configure.
Configuration of a Work Pattern
The configuration screens allow you to customise and configure work patterns and can be accessed through the Work Patterns screen by selecting the 3-dot ellipses and selecting View/Edit Work Pattern.
General Parameters
At the current time only the General Parameters screen is utilised, however as further functionality such as Rostering is introduced the other areas are likely to require configuration.
The General Parameters screen contains the main information pertaining to the Work Pattern and allows to configure for example, default hours as well as start and end time. As with all of the other screens, the Start Time, End Time and Default Hours are displayed at the top of the screen.

The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level.

Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a government-mandated payment that offers financial support to employees unable to work due to illness. SSP is calculated based on a standard 5-day workweek, but issues may arise if the system incorrectly divides it over 7 days.
This miscalculation often results from incorrect employee work patterns or system configuration errors, leading to lower SSP payments than employees are entitled to receive.
SSP payments are configured at the organizational level to use either an employee's work pattern or qualifying days.
To review this configuration, follow these steps in portal.
Click Settings, then under UK Tax Rates, click General.
If the employee's Time/Workforce Management work pattern should take precedence over the OSSP qualifying days, select the Work Pattern indicator.
If necessary, select the Qualifying Days indicator and enable the appropriate days of the week for SSP eligibility.

According to SSP guidance, an employee's average earnings must exceed the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL). The Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) is calculated based on the eight weeks prior to the start of the Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW).
To qualify for SSP, ensure that employees have an average above the LEL for the past eight weeks.
If you wish to pay the employee SSP despite their AWE being lower than the LEL, you can update the Average Weekly Earnings toggle.
To do this, follow the steps below.
Click Settings then under UK Tax Rates, click General.
From the Pay Group Code drop down menu, select the relevant pay group
Under General, turn on Average Earnings toggle.
📌Note: Enabling this option means you will pay SSP regardless of an employee's AWE, even if it falls below the LEL. This adjustment will apply system-wide and affect all employees. You cannot configure this setting for an individual employee only.
If the AWE is incorrect, check the incorrect AWE for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), as it affects all statutory sick pay calculations.
If the employee does have an average above the LEL, please raise a new case online, referencing this article's title and include the following details:
The dates for which SSP should have been generated.
The employee number.

If no salary offset appears for an employee regarding an absence recorded in CoreTime after running the future calculation of hours, generating salaries, and completing a full validation for the pay group, it likely means the employee has not been assigned an Absence/Sickness Category. Without this assignment, no sickness rule applies to the employee, and as a result, the salary will not be offset.
To assign a valid sickness category to the employee, follow the steps below in Back Office.
Click CorePay then click Employee.
Click Maintain Employee Details then click Sundry.
Click Sickness Category.
🤓Tip: If the field is blank, it indicates that the company has not set a default absence category code.
Set a default absence category code then click Save.
Re-run the validation job.
The salary offset should now be visible for the employee.

Rolled-up holiday pay ensures that employees with irregular hours or patterns receive their holiday pay spread across each pay period, rather than as a lump sum when they take their leave.
This method complies with legislation requiring holiday pay to reflect regular earnings, including overtime and bonuses, by adding a proportionate amount to each payment.
Set up rolled-up holiday pay
Create a percentage-based pay code: Create a new percentage based pay code using the pay code wizard. This should have a percentage of 12.07% to reflect the statutory calculation for allocating holiday pay.
Set up the pay code formula: When setting up the pay code specify which earnings should be considered for the holiday pay calculation. Typically, this includes all basic pay codes and any overtime pay codes. These selections ensure that the rolled-up holiday pay reflects an employee's regular earnings.
Assign to employees: Assign the pay code to your employees. Each pay period, a percentage of the designated earnings will be automatically calculated and added to their pay as rolled-up holiday pay, ensuring compliance with the legislation.
Manage Absences
To account for absences and ensure accurate holiday pay calculations:

rolled-up holiday pay, ensuring compliance with the legislation.
Manage Absences
To account for absences and ensure accurate holiday pay calculations: Download the Insight report: From the Insight report store, download the 'Irregular Paid Employees - Absence Holiday Pay Calculation' report. This report helps identify employees absent during the current pay period and provides a detailed history of their earnings over a specified period (e.g., 52 weeks) for accurate calculation.
Override ralculations: With the report's information, you can manually adjust the rolled-up holiday pay for absent employees, ensuring their holiday pay reflects their average earnings accurately.

If you enter a negate in the leave details field on the Maintain Leave Without Pay screen, you may encounter the following error:
**Start UnHandled Exception
SOURCEREF: s37000_insert_day_history
EMPNO: XXXXXX
ERRNO: -6502
ERRMESS: ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision too large.**
This error can cause the PAY140 file to fail. To troubleshoot the issue, check the `number_of_units` in the log file. If this number exceeds 999, it will indeed cause the PAY140 to fail.
Here are the steps to resolve the issue:
1. Retrieve the PAY140.trcXXXX file, where XXXX represents the pay group.
2. Review the ERRDATA row, as the system only permits values up to 999.
If the negate value is greater than 999, it is recommended to split the negate into two parts. For instance, negate half of the amount in one period and the other half in a subsequent period. This approach is necessary due to user access rights.

Click Settings, then under UK Tax Rates, click General.
Under General, enable the HR Tupe Date toggle.
Click Save.

The Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) is the European Union's initiative aimed at integrating payment systems to standardize euro transactions across participating countries. This initiative allows for seamless electronic payments using unified formats and procedures.
Organizations need to update their SEPA mode settings when they expand operations into new European markets, change banking relationships, or adapt to evolving regulatory requirements.
CorePersonnel offers three distinct SEPA modes to meet various banking requirements and operational needs:
Mode 1: Bank sort code and bank account number only.
Mode 2: Bank sort code, bank account number, BIC and IBAN.
Mode 3: BIC and IBAN only.
Initially, we place clients in Mode 2 to allow them to generate both the old bank files and the new SEPA files. Once clients are satisfied with the SEPA files, we switch them to Mode 3, as the old bank details become irrelevant.
​
Regarding Portal:
In Mode 1, users see the account and sort code.
In Mode 2, users see the account and sort code.
In Mode 3, users see the BIC and IBAN.
If you need to update the SEPA mode for all companies or for specific companies, please raise a new case online. Reference the title of this article and include details of the companies that need updating.

The pro-rata indicators on the Allowances/Payment tab of an allowance pay code play a crucial role in determining how the system calculates and applies allowances in specific scenarios.
By understanding these indicators, you can ensure accurate adjustments and compliance with Benefits In Kind (BIK) regulations, particularly when applying BIK deductions for the days an employee is available.
Understanding these settings helps ensure accurate calculations. Below is a summary of the impact of each indicator:
Pro Rata Indicator: Select this check box if the Pay Code is a Permanent/Recurring Allowance Payment which is pro-rated by the employees Contract Hours and Timesheet Basic Hours and Pro Rata Elements. By way of example if an employee's contract hours are 39 but they have only worked 20 hours then the employee will get paid 20/39 of the value of this allowance.
​
Pro Rata Element: Select this check box if this Payment is an Hourly /Daily Pay Code qualifying for the pro-rata Indicator described above i.e. the hours for this code qualify for making up the 20 hours in the example above.
📌Note: This field should only be enabled if the pay code is Hours or Days.
Pro Rata Calculation: Select this check box if the pro-rata calculation is based on the number of days the allowance is paid for. Otherwise the calculation is based on the number of days in the period.

Benefit in Kind (BIK) values are normally applied in full for each payroll period. The Pro Rata BIK feature changes this behaviour for employees who start or leave employment part-way through a period. When enabled, PeopleXD calculates a proportional BIK value based on the number of days the employee was active within that period, rather than applying the full amount.
This ensures that leavers and starters are charged an accurate BIK figure that reflects their actual days of employment, rather than a full-period charge regardless of start or leave date.
📌Note: This feature is disabled by default. Existing BIK processing is not affected until the parameter is explicitly enabled.

How it works
Pro rata is triggered for a BIK record when either:
The BIK start date is after the period start date (employee is a starter mid-period), or
The BIK end date is before the period end date (employee is a leaver mid-period).

The BIK end date is before the period end date (employee is a leaver mid-period). If neither condition is met, that is, the BIK spans the full period, the standard full BIK amount is applied, regardless of whether the parameter is enabled.
The calculation
Pro Rata BIK = (Standard BIK Value ÷ Days in Period) × Pro Rata Days
Term
Definition
Standard BIK Value
The employee's BIK value for the period
Days in Period
Total days in the payroll period (calendar or working days — see Day Basis below)
Pro Rata Days
The number of days the BIK was active within the period
Pro Rata Start
The later of: BIK start date or period start date
Pro Rata End
The earlier of: BIK end date or period end date
Pro Rata Days = (Pro Rata End − Pro Rata Start) + 1. The system automatically clamps the BIK active range to within the current period — date ranges do not need to be manually adjusted.
Example: An employee with a monthly BIK of £600 leaves on the 10th of a 30-day period. Pro Rata Days = 10, Days in Period = 30. Pro Rata BIK = (£600 ÷ 30) × 10 = £200. Without this feature, the full £600 would have been applied.

The PRSI Class Automation feature automates the update of Irish Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) classes for employees based on their age, date of birth, and State Pension Contributory (SPC) status. Without this feature, PRSI class changes for older employees must be applied manually. When enabled, PeopleXD applies the correct class transitions automatically during each payroll run.
The feature is relevant for employees aged 66 and over. Irish legislation requires that PRSI classes change from Class A or S to Class J or M depending on whether the State Pension (Contributory) has been awarded and the employee's date of birth. Frequently asked questions
What happens if an employee's SPC status changes mid-year?
The system re-evaluates SPC status and age on each payroll run. If the SPC indicator is updated on the employee record, the correct class transition will be applied from the next payroll run that processes that employee.
Can I enable this for some pay groups but not others?
Yes. Set the System Type flag to N and enable the pay group-level flag only for the pay groups where automation is required. Pay groups with the flag set to N will continue to require manual PRSI class management.
Does this affect employees under age 66?
No. The automation logic only applies to employees aged 66 and over. Employees below 66 are not evaluated and their PRSI class is not changed by this feature.
What happens when an employee turns 70?

es aged 66 and over. Employees below 66 are not evaluated and their PRSI class is not changed by this feature.
What happens when an employee turns 70? Once an employee reaches age 70, the class transition (A → J or S → M) is applied unconditionally on the next payroll run, regardless of SPC status or date of birth. This age 70 override cannot be suppressed by the SPC indicator.
How do we exclude employees who should not be transitioned?
Disable the automation at pay group level for any pay groups containing employees who require manual PRSI class management. If all affected employees are in a specific pay group, set that pay group's flag to N while leaving others enabled.
Does enabling this feature affect historical periods?
No. PRSI Class Automation applies to the current payroll period only. Previously processed periods are not reprocessed or affected.

Once the Employment Allowance EFT indicator is enabled:
Employment Allowance will appear as a line item in the Third-Party EFT listing generated for HMRC payments.
The allowance offset is applied automatically each pay period until the full annual entitlement is reached or the tax year ends.

What happens if I do not enable the indicator?
Employment Allowance will not appear in the Third-Party EFT output. Your EPS claim to HMRC will still be valid, but the EFT listing will not reflect the reduction, which may cause a discrepancy between your EFT output and the amount actually due to HMRC.
Can I enable this mid-year?

Digital Employment Verification allows your employees to share payroll data digitally with financial service providers, removing the need for manual payslip requests and giving them full control of their data and personal finances.
Access PeopleXD Payroll supports this through two provider integrations: Experian Work Report™ and The Verification Exchange® from Equifax. As an employer, you control whether this feature is active for your workforce.
Each time an employee initiates a credit application such as a credit card, mortgage, or loan, they provide consent for their payroll data to be accessed.
​
Overview
What is Digital Employment Verification?
Digital Employment Verification is the ability for employees to share their employment and income information digitally with financial service providers such as banks or mortgage lenders, directly from your payroll system. This removes the need for manual payslip requests and speeds up credit application decisions.
Access PeopleXD Payroll supports this through two provider integrations:
Experian Work Report™
The Verification Exchange® from Equifax
What does it mean for your company?

oll supports this through two provider integrations:
Experian Work Report™
The Verification Exchange® from Equifax
What does it mean for your company? A recent Experian survey of 230 Human Resources (HR) and Payroll professionals shows that many large organisations receive an average of 150 requests a month from employees to source and share payroll data. This equates to 11 hours a month of HR and Payroll team time devoted to requests.
Enabling Digital Employment Verification removes this administrative burden, reduces your carbon footprint where paper payslips would otherwise have been shared, and supports a more direct and secure way of sharing employment information on behalf of your employees.
What does it mean for your employees?
When employees apply for credit with a financial institution, they can choose to upload payslips manually or use Digital Employment Verification. If they choose the service, it automatically accesses, with their explicit consent, the required records from their employer and passes them to the provider. This delivers direct confirmation of gross and net income, employment status, and tenure in seconds.
How do employees know they can use this service?

This delivers direct confirmation of gross and net income, employment status, and tenure in seconds.
How do employees know they can use this service? Each provider maintains a list of opted-in employers supplied by Access Group. If the financial institution uses one of these providers and the employee's employer is on that provider's list, the employee is offered the option to use the service at the point of the transaction.
Is there a cost to my organisation for enabling this?
No. The integration is free for employers. There are no ongoing costs associated with enabling Digital Employment Verification for your employees.
How the integration works
What is required from my organisation to provide this service?
You enable the integration directly in your Access PeopleXD system. Once enabled, your employees can consent to a financial institution using the service to digitally share their relevant employment and income data. It is not possible to enable the integration on an employee-by-employee basis, it applies to all employees when switched on.
How does the integration work?
When the integration is enabled, the relevant data for your employees is shared with a secure holding database hosted within the Access Group UK. This database exists solely to make data available to employees who choose to use the service.

ure holding database hosted within the Access Group UK. This database exists solely to make data available to employees who choose to use the service. Only when an employee opts in with their chosen financial institution and provides explicit consent will the verification provider Experian or Equifax; access that employee's data. Access is made via a secure Application Programming Interface (API) on a one-time, transaction-by-transaction basis.
📌Note: Payslip data is held in the holding database for a rolling period of 12 months. Data older than 12 months is deleted automatically. If your organisation disables the integration, all corresponding data is deleted from the holding database.
Will there be any changes visible to end users in PeopleXD?
No. There are no employee-facing changes within Access PeopleXD Payroll. Admin users will see the parameter in Admin Settings used to configure whether the feature is enabled.
Can employees use this service if the integration is not enabled?

Can an employer enable the service for a specific provider only?

⚠️Important: The integration is only available in your live production environment. It is not available in test environments, to prevent test or dummy data from being shared with the holding database. Only enable the integration once your organisation is live-running payroll.

A priority 1 (P1) case refers to a critical issue that severely impacts business operations, such as system outages or payroll failures. You should classify a case as P1 when it meets the following criteria:
Business Critical Payroll Deadlines: The case involves a risk to a business-critical payroll deadline, and no workaround is available. Workarounds may include manual interventions.
Stalled Payroll Jobs: A payroll job is stuck, has failed, or is unavailable, jeopardizing a business-critical deadline.
Bank File Transfer Risks: There is a risk of failing to transfer the Bank file to the Bank on time.
Software or Screen Availability: The software or a specific screen is unavailable, putting a business-critical deadline at risk, and no workaround is available.
Security or Data Breach: There is a security or data breach that requires resolution from the PeopleXD Support, Development, or Product teams. While other security alerts may be high priority, only issues caused by the software can be aligned with contractual SLAs.
When logging a P1 case, please outline any affected or potentially impacted deadlines.
📌Note: Next-day deadlines may be appropriately managed under a P2 classification. Do not classify an issue as P1 if it affects only a few employees and a workaround is available (including manual timesheet input).

Display the individual rates applied during the period.
Separate the hours worked at each rate
Clearly distinguish between old and new rates, including appointments.

A PAYE reference number includes two parts:
A three-digit HMRC office number.
A unique reference number for your business, typically structured like 123/A56789 or 123/AB56789, with some exceptions.

Click Settings then click Organisations.
From the Code dropdown menu, select the relevant company.
In the Tax Office Number and District Number fields, enter the first three-digit part of the PAYE reference.
In the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields, enter the second part of the PAYE reference.

Click Save.

e Tax Office Number and District Number fields, and enter A56789 in the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields.

If the GL file does not balance with the payroll control totals report after cancellations have been made for several employees, it is likely due to a timing issue. Specifically, a cancellation payment may have been applied before the GL was run.
When a payroll period concludes, the payroll control reports display the total values for each employee for that entire period. If a cancellation occurs afterward, these payroll control reports do not update to reflect that cancellation. The complete update report (PAY355) shows the totals for all employees processed up to that point.
Subsequent cancellations do not affect the payroll controls since they occur after the reports were generated. A cancellation payment does update the employee's history in Back Office as follows:
Click on CorePay, then click Enquiry.
Click View History Details then check the employee's cumulative details.
The GL is generated from the data in the View History Details screen. If the GL is run after a cancellation, it will accurately reflect these changes.
However, if the GL was generated after the complete update but before the cancellation was recorded, the reports would balance.
📌Note: It is not possible to modify the payroll reports once the payroll process has been completed. Therefore, manual adjustments should be made to the control totals to account for any cancellations or manual payments entered.

If the above error message appears when trying to calculate and save a manual payment, this is because of a mismatch between the entered National Insurance (NI) thresholds and the total NIable pay.
NIable pay= LEL + PT + ST + UE
When the following warning appears on the screen :
"Warning: NI Thresholds not equal to NIable Pay. Only exception is for NI aggregation or where NIable Pay is below LEL. Are you sure you wish to continue?"
This is because the thresholds you entered (LEL + PT + ST + UE) do not add up to the total NIable pay. Specifically, the ‘Above UEL’ (UE) value represents the portion of NIable earnings above the Upper Earnings Limit (UEL). Including this value is essential to ensure the breakdown matches the total NIable pay.
To resolve the issue, check the employee’s tax details to view the LEL, PT, and ST limits. To do this, follow these steps in portal.
Click Employee then in the search field, search for the relevant employee.
Click View then click Tax Details.
Highlight the year.

What is an increment?
An increment is an increase or addition to an employee's pay, especially one that is part of a series based on a fixed scale.
What is the Increment Process?
This process applies only to employees who have a pay scale salary.
Increments cannot be automatically generated for those on personal rate salaries.
Using the increment process eliminates the need to manually create a salary amendment for standard annual or periodic salary increments. This process can apply to all employees or a group of employees in an organization on a common date each year.
Increments may also be applied on a date specific to the employee's post appointment, for example, 12 months from the start date or upon turning 18 or 21 years old.
When increments are processed from the CorePay side, they are generated during a payroll run and typically have a reference or reason code starting with "PAY" followed by a number indicating they were generated from CorePay.
When increments are processed from CorePersonnel, they are generated by a nightly increment job. This job usually generates increments a fixed number of days before the due date to allow HR and payroll to approve or reject them.
Key CorePersonnel increment attributes
Increment Due Date

fixed number of days before the due date to allow HR and payroll to approve or reject them.
Key CorePersonnel increment attributes
Increment Due Date This is the date on which the increment is due to be applied to the post appointment salary record. For example, if an employee starts in the organization on January 1, 2018, the employee may be due for an increment on January 1, 2019.
Managing increment due dates
You can capture the increment due date and the increment hold indicator on a salary record during the appointment stage.
These can be manually entered by the user or automatically calculated based on the terms and conditions assigned to the post appointment.
You can update the increment due date and increment hold indicator for an employee directly on the pay profile screen.
Increment details are managed at the post appointment level. The increment due date is associated with a salary record on the post appointment, not on the employee record itself.
Therefore, if an employee has multiple post appointments, it is crucial to record the increment due date for each post appointment as relevant.
Increment system job

Increment system job The CorePersonnel nightly job reviews all employees' increment due dates, creates a new salary record based on the pay scale point increment rules, and generates a new increment due date for the employee's salary. For example, if the increment due date is set for January 1, 2019, the increment system job will identify that the employee is due for an increment on that date. It will then move the employee to the next point on the scale by creating an approved salary amendment and aligning this to the employee's pay profile. The new increment due date will be updated to 12 months later, on January 1, 2020.
Increment hold indicator
This indicator ensures that the increment job does not process for the employee on the increment due date. For example, if the increment hold indicator is set against an employee's record on January 1, 2019, during the review on that date, no increment will be applied to the employee's record. However, if the increment hold indicator is removed a week later, and the increment due date is still present for January 1, 2019, the job will process it at that point, and the pay will be backdated for the seven days missed.
Pay scale point increment rules
Rules are established for each pay scale point to control:

t, and the pay will be backdated for the seven days missed.
Pay scale point increment rules
Rules are established for each pay scale point to control: The next point available.
The progression pay scale and point to be used when the maximum point has been reached on the current pay scale.
The length of time at the current point (if different from the standard 12 months).
A bar point, which stops an employee from incrementing beyond that point.
Age restrictions on progression to the next point.
Increment due date policy
The increment due date will not be removed when an employee reaches the top of the scale.
If a manual salary amendment is made to bring the employee to the top point on the scale, the increment due date will not be removed.
If bar points are used, the increment due date will also remain as the top of the scale will not be reached by the increment process.
The increment due date will only be removed if the increment process results in moving to the top point on the scale.

If an employee has both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA, the DEO will take priority over the DEA. The system will check the employee's net wage and ensure that it is equal to or greater than 60% before calculating the DEA. If the net wage falls below this threshold, the DEA will not be calculated. This means that the DEO will be deducted first, followed by the DEA.
📌Note: If the DEO deduction results in the employee receiving less than 60% of their net pay, then no DEA should be deducted.
During each pay period, People XD will evaluate the employee's net wage to determine whether the DEA deduction should be applied in full, partially, or not at all. The system has been designed in accordance with HMRC guidelines.
For further information regarding protected earnings associated with DEAs, we recommend visiting the HMRC website on Direct Earnings. This resource will help you understand what to expect in People XD concerning a DEA with protected earnings.
According to the HMRC website, here is some important information regarding protected earnings:

The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage(NMW), the National Living Wage (NLW), or the minimum apprenticeship rate. The report compares the employee’s hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age.
To check the Periodic Employee Hours setting, follow the steps below.
Click Manage Payroll then click Payroll Checking.
Click View Gross to Nett then click the Minimum Wage tab.
Turn the Periodic Employee Hours toggle on or off as needed.
📌Note: We recommend enabling Periodic Employee Hours where the contracted hours on the employee’s contract do not represent weekly hours.
For example, if the pay group uses a fortnightly pay frequency and the contracted hours stored on the contract represent fortnightly hours, the toggle should be turned on.
How the hourly rate is calculated
The calculation used in the Minimum Wage Exception report depends on whether Periodic Employee Hours is enabled or disabled.
When periodic employee hours is enabled
The hourly rate is calculated as: Hourly Rate = Pay in Period ÷ Hours at Appointment Level
Example:
Pay frequency: Weekly
Pay in period: £600
Employee hours: 40
Hourly Rate: £600÷ 40 = £15
When periodic employee hours is disabled
The system calculates the hourly rate using the following values.
Annual pay: Pay in period × annual multiplier

en periodic employee hours is disabled
The system calculates the hourly rate using the following values.
Annual pay: Pay in period × annual multiplier Weekly pay: Annual pay ÷ minimum wage report weeks
Hourly rate: Weekly pay ÷ hours at appointment level
Annual multipliers by pay frequency:
Monthly: 12
Weekly: 52
Fortnightly or bi‑weekly: 26
Quarterly: 4
Half‑yearly: 2
Check the minimum wage report weeks
​To view the minimum wage report weeks, follow the steps below in Portal.
Click Settings then click Pay Groups.
From the Pay Group Code dropdown menu, select the relevant pay group.
Click Next Page then review the Minimum Wage Report Weeks field.
📌Note: If this field is blank, the system defaults to 52 weeks.
Example (Periodic employee hours disabled)
Employee paid monthly
Pay in period: 2,600 pounds
Pay group minimum wage report weeks: 52
Employee hours: 40
Calculation
Annual pay: £2,600 × 12 = £31,200
Weekly pay: £31,200 ÷ 52 = £600
Hourly rate: £600 ÷ 40 = £15.00
For more information, check the Minimum Wage Exception report in the Minimum Wage User Guide.

If the repayment amount for the AOE or DEA deduction seems incorrect, it may be because the net earnings used in the calculation do not align with the expected formula.
For both AOE and DEA, the net earnings for an employee are calculated using the following formula:
Net Earnings = Gross Pay – Applicable Deductions
Applicable deductions include:
PAYE (Income Tax)
Employee NI/PRSI
Pension contributions
📌Note: Other deductions such as student loans, are not included in this calculation.
The deduction is then calculated using this formula:
(Lower band × lower rate%) + (Reminder (net earnings – lower band) × balance) = Deduction amount
Example
This example is based on a monthly employee.
Earnings: 2000.00
Deductions:
Pension: 100.00
PAYE: 150.00
Employee NI: 100.00
Total Deductions: 350.00
Net pay earnings used for AOE: 2000.00 – 350.00 = 1650.00
📌Note: The lower band, lower rate, and balance information can be found on the pay code used for AOE.
Lower Band: £1480
Lower Rate: 17%
Balance Rate: 50%
Deduction calculation:
Step 1: 1480 × 0.17 = 251.60
Step 2: (1650 – 1480) × 0.50 = 85.00
Total AOE Deduction: 251.60 + 85.00 = 336.60

The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) is a real-time system from the Irish Revenue that provides employers with up-to-date tax information for each employee, including tax credits, cut-off points, and USC rates.
This system automatically updates employee tax details as circumstances change, ensuring accurate tax calculations throughout the employment period.
When managing employee changes such as departures, rehires, and temporary rejoiners, it is essential to follow specific procedures to maintain tax compliance and ensure accurate tax calculations.
Leavers
When an employee leaves the organisation, the payroll submission file will notify Revenue during the employee's last pay period. Consequently, Revenue will update the employee's RPN details.
After processing a leaver in CoreHR, the employee will no longer appear in the RPN retrieval system.
Rejoiners
When rehiring an employee, there are two scenarios to consider regarding RPN based on how the rejoiner is set up in CoreHR:
Rejoin the employee with their existing employee number (recommended)
This process reactivates the existing employee record.
A rejoin date (the new start date) is recorded.
Their RPN will be retrieved using the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]).

e retrieved using the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]). The employee will not appear on the submission file with the latest start date until after their first payment.
Create a new employee record (not recommended)
If a new employee number is generated in CoreHR for the returning employee, they will be treated as a new employee.
A new employee number is created.
Their RPN will be retrieved via the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process.
A new Employment ID will be created (valid characters for Employment ID are [A-Za-z0-9_\-]).
Temporary rejoiners
The process for retrieving RPNs for temporary rejoiners differs based on whether the payroll period falls in the same year or the previous year.
For a temporary rejoiner in the same year:
Retrieve the employee RPN.
Enter the company or employee reference.
Use the most recent Employment ID for RPN retrieval; this will not be treated as new employment.
If the employee receives a payment after they have left, it will appear on the normal submission file with an end date equal to the employee's leave date and a blank start date.
📌Note: When retrieving RPNs at the employee level, the company last updated field is unavailable.
When retrieving RPNs at the company level, the employee reference will be blank, and the company last updated will default.

For a temporary rejoiner in the previous year:

Enter the company or employee reference.

Temporary rejoin or pay leavers is set.

When retrieving RPNs, there may be a scenario in which an RPN does not come in for an employee, showing an error message stating 'RPN not available for Employee'.
We have compiled a list of possible reasons to guide you on why RPNs may not be available.
Reason
Details
Employers may not have received the expected number of RPNs.
In most cases, the employer will be able to use their payroll package to identify the employees that do not have an RPN available. The following are possible reasons why an RPN may not be available along with background information and guidance to address these:
Check with the employee that the PPSN that they have provided is correct.
The Employer can use the PPSN checker on ROS to verify the PPSN and name provided matches either Revenue's or DEASP's records. The PPSN Checker is available under Additional Services on the Employer Services tab on ROS.
If you are unable to verify the PPSN using the PPSN checker, you should check with your employee that their details provided are correct.
Where an employee's individual/new PPSN is not available, the employee will need to contact DEASP to obtain the new PPSN or confirm their existing PPSN. The employee must then contact Revenue using MyAccount or the National PAYE Helpline (+353) 1 738 3636 to notify Revenue of their new PPSN.
The employee may not be registered with Revenue.

using MyAccount or the National PAYE Helpline (+353) 1 738 3636 to notify Revenue of their new PPSN.
The employee may not be registered with Revenue. While it is possible that the employee may have a valid PPSN, if the employee is not yet registered with Revenue for PAYE then neither a Tax Credit certificate nor an RPN can be issued for that employee.
​
When an employee starts their first job in Ireland, they will need to register with Revenue. This includes employees who are non-resident.
​

Revenue have recently announced that non-taxable advances will be allowed in certain scenarios.
This change is being implemented following feedback on the ERR release in relation to advanced not being allowed.
What this means?
Irish Revenue will introduce an optional administrative practice allowing the processing of non-taxable advances under certain conditions.
For example:
Conditions for Application
Advances are only allowed for anticipated travel & subsistence expenses and Employers must ensure appropriate controls are in place to track and reconcile all travel and subsistence advance payments.
Reporting Advances
Advance travel or subsistence payments must be reported under Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) using a new designated “Advances” subcategory. In addition, as the advance is drawn down on, this must also be reported to Revenue under ERR.
Reasonable Estimates
It's crucial that advance payments represent a reasonable estimate of the expected claim amount and qualify for relief under section 114 TCA 1997.
Timely Reconciliation
Employers are required to reconcile advance payments with actual claims promptly. Any excess in payment should be recouped without delay or subjected to tax if not settled.
Notification to Revenue

yments with actual claims promptly. Any excess in payment should be recouped without delay or subjected to tax if not settled.
Notification to Revenue While there's no requirement to notify Revenue in advance, employers must have appropriate governance and controls in place to meet the required conditions.
No Obligation
Employers have the discretion to opt into this administrative practice. If choosing not to, standard tax rules apply, meaning any advance payments must be taxed through payroll.
Further guidance and examples, check the Revenue Tax Duty Manual (TDM) part 38-03-33.
What do I need to do next?
Employers deciding to operate advances must report all advance travel and subsistence payments under ERR once their chosen reporting mechanism becomes available.
Revenue Manual screens:
Revenue plans to make a software change to their ROS screens to allow employers to capture and report these advance payments manually. The Revenue ROS online/file Tax and Duty Manual Part 38-03-33 upload and API are anticipated to be available within approximately two months.
PeopleXD solution:
We will be updating our software solution to accommodate the ERR reporting requirements. Until this is released, non-taxable advance payments need to be manually reported using Revenue screens.
